capacity_timeline.event: Investment announced with Gov. Beshear: $2B, 30 GWh/yr gigafactory (potential to expand to 40 GWh/yr), ~2,000 jobs, target operational by 2027. Nothing online.
Structural completion / 'topping out' milestone (final steel piece placed). Still under construction; 30 GWh target reaffirmed. No cells in production.
Construction reported continuing (infrastructure works) toward a 2027 operational date; WSJ report of a halt denied by AESC/officials. Sister SC plant paused. Still 30 GWh target, none online.

Envision AESC announces a $810m, 30 GWh gigafactory at Florence Global Technology Park, South Carolina, to supply cylindrical cells for BMW's Spartanburg plant. Described as first phase; commercial production expected 2026. Not yet under construction.
Groundbreaking held on the 30 GWh Florence County plant; construction begins. Capacity reaffirmed at 30 GWh/yr, production targeted for 2026.

March 2024 expansion announced: a second, adjacent battery facility ($1.5bn, +1,080 jobs), bringing total site commitment to $3.12bn / 2,700 jobs. Added GWh for the second facility not disclosed; the confirmed cell-plant nameplate figure remains 30 GWh/yr. (This expansion was later cancelled.)

Construction paused (~June 2025) amid EV-demand, tariff and US EV tax-credit uncertainty. The March 2024 second-plant expansion was cancelled in Feb 2025, reverting to a single ~30 GWh plant. Per late-2025 reporting the facility was ~75% complete with ~$1.2bn invested; still not operational, resumption estimated 8-12 months out.

June/July 2022 announcement: Envision AESC to build the VENERGY+ gigafactory in Navalmoral de la Mata (Caceres), planned total capacity 30 GWh/yr divided into three phases of 10 GWh each; first phase (10 GWh) originally targeted to enter operation in 2025. LFP chemistry.

Groundbreaking ceremony 8 July 2024 (presided by PM Pedro Sanchez). EUR 1 billion first-phase investment, 900 jobs; final site capacity 30 GWh/yr LFP; production scheduled to begin in 2026. Spain's first carbon-neutral gigafactory. Nothing yet operational.

August 2025 status: project advancing slowly since the July 2024 first-stone; definitive construction still pending final project submission and municipal building licence. Current first-phase proposal is two production lines totalling ~10.6 GWh/yr on the reserved 108 ha site. No capacity operational.
Nissan & AESC announce Ibaraki cell plant: initial 6 GWh/yr, ~JPY50bn, scaling to 18 GWh/yr within ~5 years on total ~JPY100bn investment. Not yet built.

First building (Gen5 lithium-ion cells) online; completion ceremony Aug 2023 with mass production from March 2024, first building began operation July 2024 at 6 GWh/yr nameplate. Supplies Nissan, Honda, Mazda.

2021 plan: expand to 18 GWh/yr within ~5 years of announcement (≈2026). Ultimate site plan later described as ~20 GWh/yr max once second and third buildings are built (no firm date). As of Sep 2025 only 6 GWh online - target not yet realised.

Tata Sons announces UK gigafactory at Gravity Smart Campus, Bridgwater, Somerset, run by new battery arm Agratas: 40 GWh/yr full nameplate, GBP4bn, production targeted from 2026. Anchor customers JLR and Tata Motors. 40 GWh is the full-site target, not an initial phase.

Production start rescheduled: full production now targeted for late 2027 (schedule slipped from 2026, grid/infrastructure upgrades cited). Capacity target unchanged at 40 GWh/yr full nameplate. Plant under construction (piling complete; steel frame of Building One completed Feb 2026). No cell capacity online. Full 40 GWh contribution described as reached by the early 2030s.
MoU signed with Gujarat government under new Electronics Policy: ~Rs 13,000 crore lithium-ion cell gigafactory at Sanand, 20 GWh/yr in phase 1. Announcement only - no construction/capacity yet.
Construction of the 20 GWh/yr lithium-ion cell plant set to begin; production targeted for 2027. No capacity online.
Construction advancing on 20 GWh/yr phase 1; structural steel framework nearing completion; production still expected 2027. Not operational.
Steel structure complete, first phase of 320-acre campus nearing completion; 20 GWh/yr phase 1; production expected to commence 2027. Still zero GWh online.

Groundbreaking / foundation stone at Divitipalli, Mahbubnagar. Amara Raja Giga Corridor announced: up to 16 GWh/yr lithium-ion CELL capacity (plus separate ~5 GWh pack assembly), Rs 9,500 crore phased over ~10 years. Nothing online yet.

60 MWh (0.06 GWh/yr) Customer Qualification Plant commissioned/inaugurated by Telangana CM on 15 July 2026 - pilot line producing cylindrical and prismatic Li-ion cells across multiple chemistries; built for ~Rs 500 crore. First actual cell capacity online at the site.
First commercial bulk cell line, 2 GWh/yr (cylindrical, NMC and LFP), targeted to begin operations by June 2027 (FY27). Not yet online as of source date.
Total cell manufacturing capacity of 16 GWh/yr targeted in phases by the end of the decade, serving automotive and storage. Future target.
Site selection announced: initial 3 GWh LFP cell facility with R&D centre and pilot line on 267 acres in Pima County; 3-6 GWh expansions planned every 6-12 months. Nothing built.

Groundbreaking (26 Oct 2023): initial factory output restated as ~5.5 GWh (5 GWh main manufacturing lines + 0.5 GWh R&D foundry-innovation line); single site to scale to 15 GWh over time. $1.2bn investment; production then expected ~2025. Still no operating capacity.

Phase-1 ~5.5 GWh full run rate now targeted for 2028; production start late 2027; construction slated to begin mid-2026; 4.5 GWh of initial output under binding offtake. As of this date construction had not yet begun and no cells produced.
Block 1 inaugurated 30 May 2023; first production line nameplate >13 GWh/yr, first cells before end-2023 with full ramp targeted end-2024. First of the site's three planned blocks.
As of early 2026 only Block 1 (~13 GWh/yr nameplate) is in production; plant hampered by 15-20% scrap rates and low pack output. Block 2 launch expected mid-2026.
Block 2 planned to roughly double site capacity to ~26 GWh/yr, commissioning mid-2026 (slipped from an original 2025 target). Not yet online as of early 2026.
Full nameplate target of 40 GWh/yr by 2030 across three production blocks, stated at inauguration.
Announced 2021 (ACC's second gigafactory, backed by a EUR 437m German government grant, Sept 2021): planned phase-1 start in 2025 with an initial capacity of 13.4 GWh. Never built.
Planned full nameplate ~40 GWh/yr (three production blocks of ~13.4 GWh each) by 2030, enabling >600,000 EVs/yr. Target only; never reached.
Construction/site preparation put on hold in June 2024 amid weak EV demand and rising costs; no cell production ever started. 0 GWh operational.
Project definitively shelved/cancelled (reported Feb 2026, ACC to unions). Site never became operational; 0 GWh ever commissioned.

ACC announces Termoli as its third European gigafactory (converting the existing Stellantis Termoli site). Planned to reach up to ~40 GWh/yr at final expansion (~2030); cell production originally targeted to start 2026. NEVER built — target only.
ACC places the Termoli (and Kaiserslautern) gigafactory project on 'standby' before any cell line is commissioned, citing weak EV demand and cost inflation. Zero cell capacity online.

ACC/Stellantis confirm the Termoli battery gigafactory is permanently abandoned (on standby since May 2024, restart prerequisites unlikely to be met). Plant never produced cells; site to be repurposed for eDCT transmissions. Cumulative online cell capacity: 0 GWh.

BAK Power (比克电池) 'Zhengzhou No.2 factory' 46-series big-cylindrical line: stated plan to reach 2.5 GWh/yr mass production by end-2024. Framed as a target across all 2024 sources; no independent source confirms it was actually online/producing at that level.
Planned big-cylindrical capacity ramp to 15 GWh/yr at Zhengzhou by end-2026 (matches the 15 GWh max first announced for the 2021 Zhengzhou large-cylindrical line, now rephased).
Planned big-cylindrical capacity ramp to 30 GWh/yr at Zhengzhou by end-2028.
Basquevolt launched as Basque solid-state initiative with target of 10 GWh/yr cell production by 2027; a pilot/prototype line planned for 2025. This is a future target, not online capacity.

A-Sample 'Cell Sample Manufacturing Plant' operational at Alava Technology Park (Minano) - a prototype/sample line producing first 20Ah cells (target 80Ah by end-2024). Sub-GWh pilot line; no GWh/yr manufacturing-capacity figure published for this line.

Plant confirmed operational, manufacturing the BQV400L Li-metal NMC cell in Spain. Still a sample/prototype-scale facility; no operational GWh/yr capacity figure disclosed. Full 10 GWh gigafactory remains a 2027 target.
Construction of the full Huzhou solid-state project begins; total planned annual capacity ~100 GWh at full build-out (CN¥40bn, 550 mu site). Long-term site target, not online.

First semi-solid-state battery cell rolls off the Huzhou line (22 Nov 2022); production start. Initial phase-1 line reported at ~2 GWh in 2022 trade reporting (conflicts with later 20 GWh Phase 1 retrospective).
Phase 1 completed September 2023 at 20 GWh/yr annual capacity (CN¥10.2bn investment); first 360 Wh/kg cells delivered to NIO end-June 2023. Matches current single-point record.
Phase 2 groundbreaking 4 July 2023, adding 20 GWh/yr (CN¥10.9bn); would bring the site to ~40 GWh once complete. Future capacity, not yet online.

Construction of the Osadano Plant (Fukuchiyama, Kyoto) began April 2009; Blue Energy JV (GS Yuasa + Honda) established 2009; investment ~JPY25bn (~US$255m); based on GS Yuasa 6Ah-class prismatic Li-ion EH6 cell; production planned to start fall 2010. Capacity stated in cells, not GWh.
Mass production of Li-ion batteries for hybrid vehicles began at the Osadano Plant (Plant No.1) in February 2011. Capacity reported in cells, not GWh.
Following a METI subsidy (awarded Nov 2012), annual production capacity for HEV and other Li-ion cells was increased to 15 million cells/year. Cells, not GWh.

As of the Feb 2020 second-plant decision, existing capacity was ~20 million cells/year. GS Yuasa announced a ~JPY20bn investment in a second Osadano plant, with construction to start within FY2020. Cells, not GWh.
Second plant (Osadano No.2) commenced operations in April 2022, adding production lines on the same Osadano site. Cells, not GWh.

Target: total capacity to reach 50 million cells/year from FY2023, via strengthened lines at the existing plant plus the new second plant (more than double the ~20M cells/yr of 2020). Announced target, cells not GWh.

Production line planned to start operating April 2027; full-scale mass production from October 2027. No specific GWh figure attached to 2027 in the source — capacity is brought online in phases toward 2030.

METI-certified 'battery supply assurance plan' (Honda / GS Yuasa / Blue Energy): new domestic plant with a planned production scale of ~20 GWh/yr for high-capacity, high-output Li-ion cells (automotive + stationary), reached via phased line start-up through 2030. Total investment ~JPY 434.1bn; up to ~JPY 158.7bn METI subsidy.
Ford and SK On announce BlueOval SK JV (Sept 2021); twin Kentucky cell plants planned at ~86 GWh/yr combined (part of $11.4bn KY+TN programme). Nothing online.
Groundbreaking on the Glendale, KY mega-campus (Dec 2022); two plants of 43 GWh/yr each (86 GWh/yr combined) under construction. Nothing online yet.

Plant 1 (Kentucky 1) commissioned; first saleable battery rolled off the line 19 Aug 2025, for the Ford F-150 Lightning. Plant 1 nameplate 43 GWh/yr now online. Second plant (further ~43 GWh/yr) not yet in production.
Full-site target of ~86 GWh/yr once Plant 2 (second 43 GWh/yr building) ramps. Timing became uncertain after the Dec 2025 Ford/SK On JV Disposition Agreement; treat as target, not online.

Site selected at Blyth (Cambois), Northumberland. GBP 2.6bn plant to be built in three phases of 10 GWh each, reaching 30 GWh/yr full nameplate by end-2027; cell production due to start Q4 2023. Nothing built at this date.
Announced target for the Blyth site revised upward to ~38 GWh/yr (from 30 GWh), reported around the POSCO Chemical cathode/materials tie-up. Still purely planned; no capacity online.

Reality check: construction halted August 2022, Britishvolt entered administration 17 January 2023. Only enabling/ground works were ever done - zero cell manufacturing capacity was ever commissioned or produced at the site.

Plant formally launched in Nanchuan Industrial Park, Xining. Phase 1 of ~10 GWh online at opening, with 7 production lines making ternary (NMC) lithium cells. Site designed for 24 GWh full production.
Design full-production nameplate of 24 GWh/yr targeted for 2019 (registered as phased 12+10+5 GWh projects), described at the time as the world's largest power-battery plant.

Xining/Qinghai base listed at 24 GWh nameplate in industry capacity roundups; second phase (~14 GWh line) converted from ternary to blade/LFP cells around Aug 2021. Base consistently cited at 24 GWh through 2022-2024.

Dec 2020: BYD (via FinDreams/Fudi) signs agreement with Bengbu municipal government, Anhui, for a new-energy power-battery base. Total planned 20 GWh/yr, investment ~CNY 6bn (~USD 917m), split into two 10 GWh phases (~CNY 3bn each). Nothing online yet.

Groundbreaking 18 Jan 2021 at Bengbu Economic Development Zone (Lingang Industrial Park). Phase 1 (10 GWh/yr) commissioned ~June 2021 per Chinese trade press. Phase 2 (further 10 GWh) broke ground Sep 2021.
Phase 2 completed (planned Q2 2022), bringing the Bengbu FinDreams base to its full 20 GWh/yr nameplate. Year-end 2022 base roundup lists Bengbu at 20 GWh operational (two-shift), online since 2021.

Groundbreaking of XCMG-FinDreams blade-battery base, Xuzhou, 4 Jan 2023; phase-1 planned 15 GWh/yr LFP blade cells (~10bn yuan total investment). Oct 2023 first power battery PACK rolled off (pack assembly, not cell lines).

By July 2024 buildings complete and first blade-battery cell line commissioned/through; all phase-1 lines (15 GWh/yr nameplate) expected fully commissioned by Oct 2024. Actual 2024 output target only >1 GWh.
Phase-1 expected to reach full annual capacity of 15 GWh/yr in 2025 (BYD/FinDreams LFP capacity reporting, Aug 2025).
Phase I (一期) online: 10 GWh/yr blade (LFP) cell line. Investment 2.8bn yuan. First production line launched Jan 2022; Phase I completed independent environmental acceptance Aug 2022.

Phase II (二期) added: 15 GWh/yr automotive power battery (lithium-ion) cells, ~320,000 sqm. EIA public notice Feb 2021, approved Mar 2022; Phase II completed phased independent acceptance May 2023. Brings total online cell capacity at the site to ~25 GWh/yr. Park output value exceeded 20bn yuan in 2023.

Zhengzhou Airport Economy Zone publishes EIA notice (12 Feb 2023) for Zhengzhou Fudi Battery Co.'s new power-battery production line: RMB 8bn investment, ~1.15 million m2, planned to reach 40 GWh/yr of blade (LFP) cells at full completion. This is a planned target, not capacity online.

First-year output: the BYD Zhengzhou (airport zone) base, which began production in April 2023, produced 7 GWh of power batteries plus energy-storage cells in 2023. This is reported production output for the base (battery + ESS combined), not a confirmed nameplate figure for the battery line alone.

Zhengzhou Airport Economy Zone discloses (25 Aug 2025) EIA acceptance for two further Zhengzhou Fudi Battery projects: a Zhengzhou Power Battery Production Line Expansion (RMB 5bn, using existing/reserved workshops in BYD's park) and a liquid-cooling-plate line. Signals expansion beyond the initial 40 GWh; no specific added-GWh figure stated in the disclosure.

Phase 1 of the Jintan base entered production (first cell output). A retrospective source claims 25 GWh design capacity, but this conflicts with the later 40 GWh three-phase total and CALB's company-wide ~11.9 GWh in 2021, so no phase-1 GWh figure is recorded as reliable.
26 Feb 2021: construction started on Phase 3, planned capacity 23 GWh/yr (under construction, not yet online at this date).

Jintan government notice: the base's Phase 4, a 30 GWh/yr lithium-ion battery project (electrode/cell/PACK workshops, 14 buildings), expected to complete and enter production in October. Stated as expected, not confirmed online.

Three phases of the Changzhou (Jintan) base fully built and in production, together forming 40 GWh/yr of power and energy-storage cell capacity. Stated in June 2025 coverage of the new 25 GWh on-site project groundbreaking and reaffirmed in Feb 2026 reporting.

Changzhou municipal government: CALB plans six manufacturing phases at the Jintan base to reach a total of 70 GWh/yr by 2025. This is the source of the ~70 GWh figure in our record - a target, not confirmed operational capacity. Publish date not confirmed (accessed 2026-07-20).
CALB unveils plan for a 50 GWh two-phase battery cell plant in Chengdu Economic Development Zone, Sichuan.
Phase 1 (20 GWh/yr, EV + energy-storage cells) completed and put into production in September 2022. This 20 GWh is the only capacity confirmed online at the site by dated sources through 2025.

Phase 2 (30 GWh/yr) groundbreaking on 25 March 2025, CNY 12bn (~$1.67bn) investment; production expected Q2 2026. Would raise the site total to 50 GWh/yr. Not confirmed operational by any dated source as of research date (2026-07).

Aug 2021: CALB signed investment agreement with Hefei/Changfeng county for a battery base at Xiatang town; ~CNY 24.8bn (US$3.8bn), ~1,250 mu, full design capacity 50 GWh/yr of power + storage cells. Nothing yet online.

8 Oct 2022: first cells rolled off the line, marking Phase 1 into production. Chinese state/local-government sources put Phase 1 at ~10 GWh/yr. (English trade press instead described Phase 1 as 50 GWh - see notes.)
Phase 2 (~10 GWh/yr) into production in March 2023 (originally targeted end-2022), bringing Phases 1+2 to ~20 GWh online; combined investment ~CNY 10bn.
Phase 3 (10 GWh/yr, ~CNY 3.5bn, signed Oct 2022): as of 17 Jul 2026 gas supply/utilities completed and preparing for commissioning in 2026. Not yet confirmed in production.

CALB signed a cooperation agreement with the Jiangmen city government (26 Jan 2022) to build a power-battery and energy-storage base at Xinhui with a planned total annual capacity of 50 GWh across two phases; total investment RMB 20bn. Construction started March 2022.
Phase I first production line commissioned; first cells rolled off the line on 23 Apr 2023 (single line online; per-line GWh not stated by source).

Jiangmen Phase I fully online: all 5 production lines in operation, Phase I nameplate 35 GWh/yr (Phase I investment RMB 13.5bn). 2023 output value exceeded RMB 2bn. Reported by Jiangmen municipal government, 27 Feb 2024.

Phase II (35 GWh/yr power + storage batteries, ~42 ha, total investment ~RMB 12bn) passed environmental-impact-assessment approval in early Jan 2026 and entered construction; expected into production June 2027, taking the site total to ~70 GWh/yr. Increment above the original 50 GWh two-phase plan.

Project officially 'landed' / environmental impact assessment for the Zhongling New Energy power-battery smart manufacturing base approved by Jinhua Wuyi ecology bureau; ¥7.5bn investment, planned annual capacity 33.6 GWh of power-battery systems, production targeted June 2026. No capacity online.

Groundbreaking / construction start on 28 Nov 2025 in Wuyi County, Jinhua. CALB 51% / Leapmotor 49% JV (Zhongling New Energy). Planned nameplate 33.6 GWh/yr; production expected June 2026. No capacity online at groundbreaking.

Announced target: full planned nameplate 33.6 GWh/yr of power-battery-system cell capacity, Phase I & II production targeted June/July 2026. This is a target, not confirmed operational as of source dates.

Meishan base (Pengshan Economic Development Zone) signed March 2022: phase 1 planned at 20 GWh power + energy-storage cells plus a 100,000 t/yr cathode-material project, total investment ~RMB 10bn. Phase 1 M2 main plant topped out 15 Oct 2022 (under construction, not yet producing).
Phase 1 (20 GWh power & energy-storage cells) entered production in 2023, per company/base capacity reviews.

Site planned total capacity 40 GWh (phase 2 adds a further ~20 GWh). No dated phase-2 commissioning/production milestone found in public sources; 40 GWh remains a planned/target figure, not confirmed online.

Groundbreaking ceremony at Sines (Zona Industrial e Logistica de Sines) on 24 Feb 2025, attended by Portugal's Economy Minister. Phase 1 nameplate target stated as 15 GWh/yr; EUR 2.065bn investment; completion targeted 2028. Under construction, no capacity online.
Phase 1 (~62,000 sqm across ~17 ha) targeted for completion within 22 months of the Jan 2026 contract, i.e. ~July 2028, at 15 GWh/yr nameplate. Still planned/under construction as of source date.

Phase 2 expansion planned from 2028 to occupy the full ~100 ha site and raise capacity from 15 to 45 GWh/yr. This is the source of the ~45 GWh figure in the current single-point record; it is a future expansion target, not online capacity.

Base signed with Wuhan Economic Development Zone (May 2021), construction from July 2021. Total planned ~50 GWh of power + energy-storage cells across four phases (~50万+ NEVs/yr). Phase I designed at 20 GWh.

Phase I main structure completed March 2022; Phase II roofed 31 May 2022 (operation expected 2023). Phase I ~20 GWh cell line completed/into production in 2022 - Wuhan's first large-scale NEV power-cell project (supplying Dongfeng et al.).
Phases I–III all completed and in operation, combined ~40 GWh/yr of power and energy-storage cells at the single Wuhan base; base 2025 output value exceeded RMB 10bn.

Phase IV project (started July 2025, +RMB ~1.2bn) is a battery PACK assembly line - 6 lines, ~400,000 packs/yr - NOT additional cell capacity; mass production expected 2026. Full four-phase base targeted at ~50 GWh / 600,000 NEVs.
Phase 1 commenced production at end of 2020. Phases 1 and 2 together = 20 GWh and Phase 2 is stated at 10 GWh, implying Phase 1 ~10 GWh.
Phase 2 groundbreaking on 2 March 2021, targeting 10 GWh/yr. Not yet online, so cumulative online capacity unchanged.
Phase 2 (10 GWh) completed whole-line equipment commissioning and started full-line feeding on 30 August 2022.

Phase 3 Stage 1 (10 GWh, first tranche of the 40 GWh Phase 3) scheduled operational Q1 2023 (Gasgoo). April 2026 reports confirm the Xiamen base has 30 GWh built and in production, consistent with Phase 1 (10) + Phase 2 (10) + Phase 3 Stage 1 (10).

New 15bn RMB high-performance lithium battery project (30 GWh planned, = Phase 3 Stages 2 and 3) formally broke ground on 5 February 2025; on completion the Xiamen base reaches 60 GWh/yr. No new capacity online yet.
Phase 3 Stage 2 (20 GWh, 5 lines) in trial production as of April 2026, with formal launch expected May 2026. Not yet confirmed as in mass production.

Phase 3 Stage 3 (10 GWh) construction began late March 2026, topping-out expected September 2026, production expected March 2027. Brings Xiamen base to its full 60 GWh/yr nameplate across three phases.

Groundbreaking 10 Jan 2026 in Yudongnan High-Tech Zone, Henan; RMB 9.63bn total investment; 51 GWh power + energy-storage cell lines planned; production planned to start Oct 2026 (no per-phase GWh figure published).
Full capacity (达产) of 51 GWh targeted for January 2028 per the project announcement.

CALB signs JV agreement with Handan municipal government to build a 51 GWh/yr power & energy-storage battery base; total investment ~RMB 10bn, JV registered capital RMB 4bn (CALB 60% / Handan SOE 40%). Full-base target announced; nothing yet built.
Phase 1 project filing (备案) approved for CALB Technology (Handan): 12 GWh/yr power & ESS cells, ~RMB 5.4bn Phase 1 investment. First tranche of the 51 GWh base.

Construction milestone: M1 electrode workshop and M2 cell workshop main structures topped out; first high-precision coating machines arriving, transition to equipment-installation phase; Phase 1 (12 GWh/yr) targeted to start production September 2026, full base 51 GWh/yr on completion. Still under construction, no cells produced yet.

Camel Group (骆驼股份) announces 6.8bn yuan Xiangyang new-energy low-carbon industrial park: full plan = 10 GWh/yr energy-storage lithium battery base + 12M units/yr low-voltage lithium, split into two phases. 10 GWh is the full-build target, not online.

Phase 1 broke ground 28 Jul 2023: planned 2 GWh/yr energy-storage lithium + 4M units/yr low-voltage lithium (3.3bn yuan), targeted for full operation by end-2024. Phase 2 planned 8 GWh ESS + 8M units. Target only — see 2025 status.

H1 2025 report: Phase-1 first production line in normal production (low-voltage lithium line completed build & debug end-2024); new soft-pack PACK workshop still under construction. No GWh of energy-storage cell capacity confirmed operational.

CATL announces its 2nd European plant in Debrecen: EUR 7.34bn investment, full-site nameplate target 100 GWh/yr, construction of first facilities to start in 2022, build period not exceeding 64 months. No capacity online yet.

Phase 1 cell factory = 40 GWh/yr, reported construction complete and machines installed, capacity fully booked by clients; series cell production targeted for March/April 2026. Full site to reach 100 GWh in later phases. Still a target - cells not yet in production at this date.

As of June 2026 CATL is still sourcing battery cells from its Chinese plants because cell production in Debrecen has NOT begun (project several months behind schedule; awaiting final permits before test then series production). Confirmed operational CELL capacity = 0 GWh. Only a ~5 GWh module/pack assembly line is running on-site (out of cell scope).

Dongying municipal government and CATL sign strategic cooperation agreement (15 March 2025) to build CATL's first high-proportion green-power direct-supply zero-carbon industrial park; Phase 1 = 40 GWh lithium battery green intelligent manufacturing base in Kenli District, built to 'zero-carbon factory + lighthouse factory' standard. Nothing online yet.

Phase 1 40 GWh base broke ground / on-site construction launched 26 July 2025 (China's first 100% green-power direct-supply zero-carbon industrial park); reported as expected to be completed and put into operation 'next year' (2026). Under construction, not yet producing as of source date.
Phase 1 (No.1 factory) begins cell production on 22 Dec 2021; phase-1 nameplate 60 GWh/yr, planned base total 120 GWh. RMB17bn phase-1 investment.
Cell factories No.1-4 plus module factory all in production by September 2022; total capacity exceeds 85 GWh/yr.
No.5 gigafactory construction started 21 Oct 2024; 25 GWh/yr planned, intended to lift base to 110 GWh. Under construction, not yet online.
No.5 gigafactory expected to begin production August 2025, which would raise base capacity to 110 GWh/yr. Target only - as of May 2026 not confirmed in production.
As of 9 May 2026, four cell factories (No.1-4) plus module factory commissioned; total capacity still exceeds 85 GWh/yr. No.5 (to reach 110 GWh) described in future tense, i.e. not yet in production.
Phase 6 expansion announced May 2026: RMB5bn ($735m) to add 40 GWh/yr sodium-ion capacity over a 24-month build, lifting planned base total to 149 GWh.
Phase 1 investment agreement (30 GWh EV + ESS) signed in Gui'an New Area in Nov 2021; construction began early 2022. Site master plan = 60 GWh across two phases. Nothing online yet.

Phase 1 commissioned / inauguration ceremony held 27 Oct 2023 in Gui'an New Area. Designed annual capacity 30 GWh EV + ESS cells (~885 mu, ~RMB7bn), 95% automation, 'one cell per second'. First and to date only operational capacity at the site.

Phase 2 investment cooperation agreement (30 GWh power & ESS batteries, ~550 mu) signed between Gui'an New Area and CATL in early Jan 2026, built on the operational Phase 1. Would take the site to its full 60 GWh plan. Planned/announced only — not yet under construction or online as of the source date.

Phase I officially commenced production (mid-May 2025); Phase I total scale stated as 60 GWh/yr. CATL's first production base in northern China, Yanzhou District, Jining City, Shandong. Multiple sources (electrive 2025-05-21, SMM/metal.com, sina 2025-05-17) corroborate the 60 GWh Phase I figure and May 2025 start.

Phase II (three production lines, ~60 GWh/yr) reported completed/coming online, taking the site to ~120 GWh/yr. NOTE date/figure uncertainty: this k.sina piece ('largest northern base, Phase II to be commissioned this month', month-precision April 2026) and English trade press (SMM, Gasgoo) put Phase II online ~April 2026, while some earlier Chinese reporting cited a December 2025 Phase II target; Phase II is treated here as operational as of mid-2026. Lower confidence on exact timing.

Full three-phase plan: total planned capacity 160 GWh/yr (power and energy-storage batteries), total investment ~14 billion yuan. Phases II and III scheduled across 2025-2026; full 160 GWh is the announced end-state target (year shown as ~2027 end-state, not a dated online figure). This is the figure the single-point record (~160 GWh) reflects.
Jiangsu Time (Liyang) plant in early production (began ~June 2018, ~1-2 GWh initial); ~5 GWh/yr cited for 2019, initial phase. Soft single-source figure.

Phase 4 (40 GWh/yr, 12 lithium-ion lines) first products off the line (29 Dec 2021), raising the Liyang base total to ~126 GWh/yr. Announced Feb 2021 by Argus; commissioning confirmed by Liyang municipal government.
Liyang plant named a WEF Global Lighthouse factory (Dec 2023); operational capacity cited at 126 GWh/yr.

LY7 project (60 GWh/yr, Kirin cells; CATL wholly-owned Jiangsu Time New Energy) entered production 29 Aug 2025. Cumulative 186 is derived (126 prior base + 60 LY7); no source states the post-LY7 total directly.
LY8 project (40 GWh/yr) construction started Aug 2025 - not yet online.
LY9 / phase III project (60 GWh/yr, ~10bn RMB) signed 27 Nov 2025 - future phase, not yet online.
Phase 1 (30 GWh/yr; 3 cell + 10 pack lines) put into operation; plant reported operational July 2024, cell production line officially in production November 2024
Phase 2 (further 30 GWh/yr; 3 cell + 10 pack lines) officially put into production Sept-Oct 2025; phases I+II total 60 GWh/yr online
Four-phase base planned to reach ~120 GWh/yr; phases 3 & 4 (reported 60% and 25% complete) targeted for completion by October 2026

Fuding base (one of CATL's Ningde-city bases) began cell production 21 Dec 2021 with 60 GWh/yr phase 1; construction had started 2 Mar 2021. This is a single sub-base within the hub, not the whole-hub total.
Fuding base full planned nameplate of 120 GWh/yr when both phases complete (phase 1 = 60 GWh online Dec 2021).

CATL's production bases across Ningde city reported at a combined 330 GWh/yr total capacity as of end-2025 (multi-base HUB aggregate, not a single plant), with a further ~170 GWh under construction or planned.

Aug 2021: CATL signs a cooperation agreement with Shanghai's Lin-gang Special Area / Lingang Group. Reuters and trade press report a planned cell plant of up to 80 GWh/yr. This 80 GWh figure is a rumoured/announced target from sources close to the deal and was NEVER officially confirmed by CATL.

19 Feb 2022: groundbreaking of the new 2.8bn yuan (~USD 440m), ~350,000 sqm Lingang plant intended to make cells 'everything under one roof' (unlike the earlier co-located leased site that only assembles modules and does not make cells). Reported to complete/enter operation within ~1 year. No cell-capacity figure officially disclosed at groundbreaking.

Phase 1 (一期) of the Xiamen Times New Energy battery industrial base breaks ground in Tongxiang High-tech City (同翔高新城), Tong'an, Xiamen. Investment up to 13bn yuan; planned 60 GWh/yr of power + energy-storage cell lines. Nothing online yet.

As of mid-Oct 2023, Phase 1 stage-1 buildings handed over to production departments; trial production expected by year-end 2023. Source gives no confirmed online-GWh split, so no cumulative figure recorded.
Phase 1 stage-2 (completing the 60 GWh) under accelerated construction, expected full delivery/handover by end-2025 (per July 2025 status of Xiamen's four battery projects, total 33.9bn yuan).
Phase 2 (二期), a separate 30 GWh/yr power-battery line (entity 厦门时代新能源动力科技, est. Aug 2025; construction from Apr 2025), targets trial production in Q2 2026, taking the base to ~90 GWh/yr.

Phase 1 (一期) of Qinghai Times New Energy at Nanchuan Industrial Park, Xining — CATL's first domestic production base — entering production: 1.5 GWh/yr power and energy-storage lithium batteries, ~1.9bn yuan invested. Project broke ground Aug 2012.

Site has built 8 production lines, reaching an annual operational scale of 10.5 GWh/yr of power and energy-storage lithium batteries (cumulative ~5bn yuan invested, 2000 mu). Per Qinghai provincial government feature.

15 GWh power and energy-storage battery project (technical-renovation / 技改) landed in 2024, with production targeted for around August 2025. Separately, a 500m-yuan electrode (极片) plant broke ground 23 Jul 2025. Whether the 15 GWh adds to or rebuilds the existing 10.5 GWh is not stated.
Phase 1 (first section) commissioned at ~15 GWh/yr; total base then planned across six phases.
Sichuan Times phases 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 reported commissioned, ~125 GWh/yr online (moderate confidence, trade-press).
Phase 7 (Times Chang'an, part of ~50 GWh phases 7-8) put into production June 2023; first plant commissioned in the Changjiang industrial park. Base-wide cumulative total not stated for this date.
Seven factories operational (Sichuan Times phases 1,2,3,5,6 + Times Geely + Times Chang'an) totalling 180 GWh/yr; base output surpassed 100bn yuan.
Times Chang'an phase-1 expansion (30 GWh/yr) commissioned 10 Nov 2025, lifting base operational capacity from 180 to 210 GWh/yr.
Target: with phases 8 and 9 commissioning and all 11 Yibin factories complete, base capacity to reach 300 GWh/yr in 2026 (planned, not yet online).

Groundbreaking (奠基) 28 Oct 2021 of the Yichun Times (宜春时代) battery base in Yichun Economic Development Zone; phase 1 investment ¥13.5bn, planned 50 GWh/yr nameplate. Construction officially started 24 Dec 2021.

Official project plan (as reported Sep 2022): phase-1 base (50 GWh/yr) to begin trial production Mar 2023 and reach full production (达产) Jun 2023; phase-1 plant 1 (一期一厂) design capacity ~32 GWh/yr. Projected annual revenue ~¥50bn at full build. Trade reports place plant 1 trial production around mid-2023.
Xinhua/government retrospective states the base's capacity had expanded from 50 GWh/yr to over 70 GWh/yr by end-2024, with annual output value exceeding ¥5bn. (>70 GWh recorded conservatively as 70.)
CATL announces Guangdong/Zhaoqing base: phase 1 designed at 25 GWh, RMB 12bn (US$1.9bn) investment; part of a wider Guangdong-province-wide 150 GWh target by end-2030 (province-wide, not this site).
Ruiqing Times phase-1 'factory one' (一工厂) formally into production on 30 May 2022; 25 GWh design capacity. Construction began 28 Mar 2021; ~14 months to production.

Phase 2 (二阶段) groundbreaking on 24 Dec 2023 in Zhaoqing High-tech Zone — full-chain energy-storage expansion (cells to boxes/cabinets/containers), completion targeted end-2024. No GWh capacity figure disclosed.
Phase 2 pre-process handover and equipment-installation ceremony held 13 Jan 2025; phase 2 still not in production. No incremental online capacity confirmed and no GWh figure disclosed.

Thuringia environment ministry handed CATL the permit for an initial 8 GWh/yr (April 2022); serial cell production kicked off at Arnstadt/Erfurter Kreuz in December 2022 - CATL's first plant outside China.
Plant formally inaugurated end-January 2023 at its full designed annual capacity of 14 GWh/yr (EUR 1.8bn investment). Cells supply VW Group PPE models (Porsche Macan, Audi Q6 e-tron).

CATL confirmed it is still ramping utilisation at Arnstadt against the 14 GWh/yr design capacity ('working at high capacity to fulfil customer requirements'); no expansion of nameplate beyond 14 GWh reported.
CATL signs/plans Luoyuan new energy battery base, planned annual capacity 40 GWh (project contract signed 2 Jan 2025)
Phase I construction officially begins 24 Apr 2025; 6.5bn yuan, ~900 mu, planned 40 GWh/yr of Li-ion cell lines (not yet online)
Targeted completion and start of operation mid-2027 at 40 GWh/yr (first factory delivery targeted Oct 2025, full construction by end-2025)

50:50 CATL-Stellantis JV announced (up to €4.1bn) to build an LFP cell/module gigafactory at Stellantis' Figueruelas (Zaragoza) site; 'up to 50 GWh' nameplate targeted, to be built in several phases; production targeted by end of 2026. Nothing online.

Groundbreaking / construction start of the JV (branded 'Contemporary Star Energy'); still targeting up to 50 GWh LFP; construction expected to conclude by March 2028. No capacity yet online (site under construction).

Phase 1 into production on 15 Dec 2020 using BYD's first 6th-generation blade (LFP) cell line at the Ningxiang High-tech Zone base. Base design nameplate 10 GWh/yr; sourced first-year cell capacity ~4 GWh (ramping). Day-one output ~50,000 blade cells/day.
Phase 1 ramping through 2021; Changsha Evening News reports output value expected to exceed RMB 10bn the following year. No dated per-year GWh figure published for 2021 (not interpolated).

Hunan provincial industry authority reports Changsha FinDreams phase-1 cell lines running at basically full capacity (~10 GWh/yr nameplate, 4 cell lines); phase 2 under construction. Output value exceeded RMB 10bn in 2022.

2025 trade-press coverage still describes the Ningxiang cell base as a ~10 GWh/yr, 4-cell-line blade-battery plant. Separately, a PACK-line expansion (+19 GWh battery PACKS, not cells) received environmental approval in Apr 2025 - pack assembly, excluded from cell capacity.

Xiaogan Lithium Battery Industrial Park broke ground (May 2022) in Linkong Economic Zone, Xiaogan, Hubei. Planned full build-out 150 GWh/yr across 5 phases; total investment CNY 67.5bn. Figure is the announced park target, not online capacity.
Phase 1 officially put into production on 28 June 2023, with a designed annual capacity of over 30 GWh of lithium-ion cells for power and energy-storage batteries.
CBAK announced plan to invest RMB50M to add one production line of 0.4 GWh/yr (model 26650, +100,000 cells/day) at the Dalian plants.
As of 31 Dec 2023, Dalian had three model-26-series production lines with total annual capacity of 1.0 GWh/yr (operating at full capacity into 2024).

New model 40135 production line (~2.3 GWh/yr) launched/commissioned at Dalian on 15 Oct 2025, added to the existing 1.0 GWh from three legacy 26-series lines, giving a nameplate of ~3.3 GWh/yr (ramp to full utilisation expected by early 2027).
Dalian site reported running at 3.3 GWh/yr.
Dalian site stated to be expandable to a maximum of ~16 GWh/yr (future target, not online).

Groundbreaking of the 20 GWh lithium battery project by Guangxi Ningfu New Energy (DFD/Do-Fluoride New Energy, stock 002407) in Lingli/Lingxi Industrial Park, Qingxiu District, Nanning. ~RMB 10.16bn total; originally planned in three phases of 6 + 4 + 10 GWh. Nothing online yet - target figure only.

Phase 1 (5 GWh/yr, ~RMB 2.9bn) completed and put into production in November 2022, producing prismatic and cylindrical cells for EV, ESS and light-EV markets. (Original announcement had called Phase 1 6 GWh; the built/operational line is stated as 5 GWh - conservative figure taken.)
Phase 2 (15 GWh/yr, ~RMB 7.3bn) broke ground 27 September 2023; on completion the Nanning site reaches its full 20 GWh nameplate. Under construction as of this date - not yet online.

Factory 1 and Factory 2 reported in operation with combined ~20 GWh; final ~10 GWh cylindrical-cell line was in equipment debugging, expected to commence operation by end February 2026, roughly doubling the site's cylindrical capacity. Lines reported running 24h at >95% utilisation with saturated order book (Jan 2026).

DFD's lithium battery capacity stood at ~3.5 GWh, concentrated at the Jiaozuo (Henan) base; the Guangxi Nanning base first phase (5 GWh) had not yet been commissioned at this point, so the existing operational cells were essentially all at Jiaozuo. (Product mix: pouch, cylindrical and prismatic; later pivoted to large-cylindrical.)

By end-2025 DFD's new-energy battery capacity reached 20 GWh, split 10 GWh at Jiaozuo (Henan) and 10 GWh at Nanning (Guangxi). A new ~5.5 GWh large-cylindrical line was added at the Jiaozuo base during the ramp. This 10 GWh figure is the Jiaozuo-specific portion.
First module planned production start (originally Q2 2026); module GWh not specified in source
Full-scale nameplate target of ~40 GWh/yr across three modules; LFP, nickel/cobalt-free
~40 GWh full-scale target reaffirmed; Morlus Technology partnership to accelerate build, final investment decision targeted 2025

Groundbreaking / first-stone ceremony on 6 July 2026; construction begins on the Brindisi LFP cell + module gigafactory (Eni Storage Systems, a JV of Eni Industrial Evolution and FIB / Seri Industrial). No capacity online at this date.

Announced full-nameplate target for the Brindisi site: ~8 GWh/year of LFP cell + module production (half of the combined 16 GWh/year Brindisi + Teverola hub) by 2030. Phase 2 later adds LFP cathode active material and battery recycling on the same site.
Phase 1 (10 GWh) commissioned: first batch of ternary (NMC) cells rolled off the line on 8 November 2024 and exported; Phase 1 investment ~7bn yuan.
Phase 2 (20 GWh power + ESS cells) construction started 28 Feb 2025, expected production 2026, taking the site to a planned 30 GWh total. NOT yet online.

EIB confirms EUR 450m financing for the Douai gigafactory. Initial (phase 1) capacity planned at 9 GWh/yr powering ~200,000 EVs, with three planned expansions to reach 24 GWh/yr (up to 30 GWh/yr) by 2030. Nothing online yet.

Start of production / official inauguration on 3 June 2025 (President Macron attending). Phase 1 online with initial annual nameplate capacity of ~10 GWh (earlier planning figure was 9 GWh), supplying cells for the Renault 5 E-Tech. Note: full phase-1 output not reached at launch - real ramp to full ~10 GWh targeted around end-2027; ~70,000-75,000 vehicles' worth of cells targeted for 2026. cumulative_gwh here is the phase-1 nameplate online, not achieved output.

Announced target: expansion via three phases to 24 GWh/yr (some reporting cites up to 30 GWh/yr) by 2030. Future/announced - not online. Recent reporting notes European auto-market slowdown may delay these expansions.

Phase 1 commissioned April 2022 - one power-battery line plus two energy-storage lines, prismatic LFP, 10.5 GWh/yr. Described as the largest single operational battery plant in northern China; first net-zero battery park.

Phase 2 (20 GWh/yr: electrodes, cells, modules, packs) signed 14 April 2023 and broke ground 27 April 2023, taking total site nameplate to 30.5 GWh. Announced/under construction - no confirmed commissioning date found.

As of Q1 2025 the site's operational Phase 1 (10.5 GWh) remained the running base; company reported a Q1 2025 line/product upgrade lifting per-cell capacity ~12.5% (energy density, not added GWh nameplate). No source confirms Phase 2's 20 GWh online, so operational floor stays 10.5 GWh.

Project signed/announced: Envision AESC Zero-Carbon Smart Battery Industrial Park, Shiyan (Hubei). Total planned 40 GWh/yr in two phases; Phase 1 = 20 GWh/yr. RMB 12bn investment. Groundbreaking April 2022; targeted same-year start.
Phase 1 (20 GWh/yr) ramped to full production. First prismatic line online mid-2023; all 7 lines reported to reach full production by end-2023, with ramp-to-full time cut from ~4 months to ~40 days.
Shiyan base confirmed at full production of its 20 GWh/yr Phase 1 nameplate (~60,000 cells/day), annual output value exceeding RMB 10bn. No Phase 2 online yet.
July 2021 announcement of second Sunderland plant; production to begin with 9 GWh/yr (Nissan/AESC/UK govt announcement).
Groundbreaking/foundation-laying ceremony (Dec 2022); expected capacity at launch 12 GWh/yr, with future potential discussed up to ~35 GWh.
Gigafactory commenced battery cell production on 16 December 2025; initial nameplate capacity 15.8 GWh/yr (enough for ~200,000 EVs/yr).
Envision AESC announces a 20 GWh/yr lithium-ion battery cell plant in Jiangyin (northern Wuxi), Jiangsu, structured as a three-phase project. Announcement/planned figure, no phase online yet.
Phase 1 (5 GWh/yr) commissioned and in mass production at the Wuxi/Jiangyin base since 2021. Some reporting cites ~3 GWh as initial actual output versus the 5 GWh phase-1 nameplate.

Phase 2 groundbreaking on 7 Feb 2022 in the Jiangyin Lingang Development Zone; ~15 GWh/yr additional planned capacity, ~10bn yuan investment, targeted for completion/production in 2023, taking the base to 20 GWh/yr total.

As of Aug 2024 only Phase 1 (5 GWh) is confirmed in mass production; the Phase 2 (15 GWh ternary/NMC) factory building is erected but still undergoing completion-acceptance, i.e. not yet producing. The original 2023 target for the full 20 GWh had slipped.

Phase 1 groundbreaking (2025-10-27): 40 GWh energy-storage cell super factory (700+Ah cells), full lithium-battery chain, targeted for production in 2026. Not yet online at this date - figure is the phase-1 nameplate target.

Phase 1 commissioned: 40 GWh lithium-battery (energy-storage) project put into operation at commissioning ceremony on 2026-07-15; 790Ah large-format storage cell rolled off the line, first batch shipped to Germany. Took under a year from Oct 2025 groundbreaking to production.

Phase 2 groundbreaking (2026-04-23): 60 GWh new-generation storage cells + 60 GWh AI energy-storage systems, targeted for full operation in 2027. With Phase 1's 40 GWh this makes the site a ~100 GWh-level cell base (plus 60 GWh system assembly) - billed as the world's first 100 GWh-class full-chain energy-storage base. Cell nameplate 40+60=100 GWh; the 60 GWh system line is pack/system assembly, not additional cell capacity.

Framework agreement with Chengdu Economic Development Zone to build a 50 GWh/yr power & energy storage battery base plus the Chengdu research institute, in two phases (Phase 1: 20 GWh, Phase 2: 30 GWh), total investment CNY 20bn on a ~1,000 mu (66.7 ha) site. Announced target only, nothing built yet.

Groundbreaking held 30 March 2023 in Longquanyi district, Chengdu (CNY 10bn agreed investment). The initial phase was scaled up from 20 GWh to 30 GWh: ~9 GWh of high-capacity/high-rate 21700 storage cells + ~21 GWh of 46-series large-cylindrical power cells. This is construction start, NOT operational capacity.
Base established; first battery line (~3 GWh). Retrospective figure stated in 29 Jul 2025 provincial feature ('capacity surged from 3 GWh to 169 GWh over 13 years').
~11 GWh operational at Jingmen per June 2021 phased-expansion disclosure (a further 11 GWh under construction, 82.5 GWh planned; total plan 105.5 GWh).
28.5 GWh operational per Nov 2021 revised plan; 124.11 GWh planned/under-construction on top, giving a 152.61 GWh total-capacity target (CNY30.5bn total investment).
Zones 6-9 (73 GWh, CNY16.6bn) put into production at ceremony on 1 Feb 2023; the 60 GWh superfactory broke ground the same day.
5 Nov 2024: announced a 152.61 GWh/yr Jingmen power & storage battery industrial-park project, fixed-asset investment CNY30.521bn.

10 Dec 2024: 60 GWh superfactory (zone 10, MB56 / 628Ah LFP ESS cells) Phase I into production; Phase-I line design capacity 17 GWh (stated '>15 GWh'). Officials cited a 212 GWh Jingmen-base target at full build-out.
Jingmen base cumulative capacity stated at 169 GWh across 18 factory buildings (13 years, annual output value >CNY40bn).
Jingmen base target 212 GWh once the 60 GWh superfactory is fully commissioned.

Jiangsu EVE-Linyang Energy Storage Technology JV formed (Hubei EVE Power 65% / Linyang Energy 35%), investing up to CNY 3bn to build a 10 GWh/yr LFP storage-cell base at Qidong; groundbreaking June 2021.
EVE-Linyang 10 GWh/yr storage-dedicated LFP cell project officially built and put into production on 18 Nov 2022; three high-speed cell lines, phase-1 investment CNY 3bn (equipment CNY 1bn).

EVE Energy signed the investment framework to scale the Qujing (Yunnan) site up from the earlier 10 GWh plan to a 23 GWh/yr cylindrical LFP energy-storage & power-battery project - six lithium-ion cell lines (150ppm each), total investment ~CNY5.5bn, ~500 mu, 18-month build. This 23 GWh is the announced full nameplate, not capacity online.
Yunnan provincial energy-conservation review (节能审查) for the 23 GWh Qujing cylindrical LFP project passed - a dated construction-approval milestone; still 23 GWh planned, nothing yet online.

First of six production lines completed and put into production at the Qujing site (reported operational by July 2024). Per-line GWh not directly stated by the source; ~3.8 GWh is a pro-rata of the officially stated 23 GWh over the officially stated six lines - treat as the achieved floor for one line online.

Lines 2 and 3 reported as expected to enter trial production 'end of 2024 / early 2025'; remaining lines toward the full 23 GWh nameplate. Announced/expected schedule - no dated source confirming these lines actually operational, so not counted as online.
EVE Energy announces RMB 10 billion investment to build a power and energy-storage battery R&D and manufacturing base in Shenyang Economic Development Zone; total planned annual capacity 40 GWh/yr.
Groundbreaking ceremony held 20 March 2023; construction of the 40 GWh planned base begins (nothing online yet).

Shenyang base officially launches operations on 30 June 2025 (pilot-project trial production + systems factory commissioned + cold-climate battery research centre). First phase provides 20 GWh/yr for power and energy-storage batteries; full base still targeting 40 GWh/yr.

Phase I cylindrical (21700-format) line commissioned - first cell rolled off the line 16 Feb 2025. Nameplate 680 million 21700 cells/yr, equating to just over ~10 GWh/yr. Cells for power tools and e-two-wheelers.

Phase II energy-storage battery plant (628Ah large ESS prismatic cells) completed / put into operation late Feb 2026, adding a planned 10 GWh/yr. Site enters large-scale production; cumulative ~20 GWh/yr across Phase I + II.

EVE Energy announced (17 May 2022) an investment agreement with the Yuxi High-tech Development Zone (Longquan area) to build a 10 GWh power and energy-storage battery project; total investment RMB 3bn (RMB 2.1bn fixed assets), ~500 mu of land, to be run by a dedicated Yuxi subsidiary. Announced target only.

Project's planning/construction permit entered the public-notification (approval) stage in Yuxi High-tech Zone, Longquan area. Scope: cell workshop, formation workshop, consumer-AI battery workshop, structural-parts workshop; two high-performance Li-ion lines plus multiple consumer-AI battery lines; ~370,723 m2 site; annual output of 10 GWh 'and above' at full production. Still pre-construction / not operational.
Phase 1 nameplate set at 6 GWh/yr; company seeking additional land to eventually expand the site to 12 GWh/yr. Nothing online.
Project structured in two phases; Phase 1 of 6 GWh/yr targeted for completion by FY25 (~Rs 5,000 cr incl. module/pack). Under construction, no cells produced.

Phase 1 (6 GWh/yr) in final commissioning; first customer samples dispatched in Q1 FY27; first commercial revenue expected Q3 FY27 (LFP for telecom/BESS/EV), ~3 GWh of the 6 GWh line to be utilised in FY27. Not yet in commercial production.
Full-site build-out target of 12 GWh/yr (Phase 2 doubling of the 6 GWh Phase 1). No date confirmed for Phase 2 capacity coming online.
Teverola 1 launched — Italy/Southern Europe's first lithium cell plant; ~0.3 GWh/yr pilot line producing soft-pouch LFP (50 Ah) cells.

Teverola 1 fully operational at 0.350 GWh/yr, producing and selling cells on the market; serves as pilot for Teverola 2. Teverola 2 equipment installation underway (~EUR 200m of ~EUR 505m invested as of 31 Dec 2025); not yet producing.

Teverola 2 gigafactory target: +8 GWh/yr of LFP prismatic BESS cells at full nameplate (production start 2026, full capacity 2027), on top of Teverola 1's 0.35 GWh. IPCEI-backed, ~EUR 417m+ public funding.

30 GWh two-phase new energy battery base announced for Ganzhou, Jiangxi; phase 1 (initially reported ~18 GWh NCM pouch, later defined as 15 GWh SPS soft-pack LFP), phase 2 to 30 GWh total. Construction commenced 2022.

Phase 1 first trial products rolled off line (Q1 2024, March); material feeding from Q2 2024; roll-off ceremony 20 May 2024. Some production lines operational and shipping, but online capacity NOT quantified in GWh (online-unquantified).

Phase 1 (15 GWh SPS soft-pack LFP) target to reach full intended-operational state by Dec 2025, delayed from originally planned Feb 2025 (announcement 2025-008). As of 2025 half-year report only partial lines operational; 15 GWh is a target, not yet online.

Farasis announces a 30 GWh/yr power battery base in Sino-Singapore Guangzhou Knowledge City, Huangpu district; LFP and ternary cells, built in two phases. Full 30 GWh nameplate is the announced site target (full production expected ~2025).
Phase 1 (15 GWh/yr) started trial production on 29 Jun 2024 - LFP SPS large-pouch cells; first pile driven 1 Sep 2023 (built in ~10 months). Line ramp-up beginning, not yet at full utilisation.

Farasis adjusts (delays) the date for the Guangzhou 30 GWh base Phase 1 (15 GWh) to reach its designed usable/operational state to Q4 2025 (December 2025); some lines installed and in production, others still being commissioned due to infrastructure delays.

Groundbreaking of Farasis Energy's Zhenjiang power-battery base (Dagang New District, Zhenjiang, Jiangsu), Oct 2018. Total investment ~RMB15bn, planned in two phases for 20 GWh/yr, with phase 1 (16 GWh target) due for completion 2019 and commissioning 2020. Plant later restructured into three ~8 GWh phases (24 GWh).

As of 30 Sept 2021 (STAR Market private-placement filing), Farasis' total online capacity was ~13 GWh/yr, comprising ~5 GWh at Ganzhou and ~8 GWh from Zhenjiang phase 1. So the Zhenjiang site had roughly 8 GWh/yr of ternary pouch cell capacity in production.

Aug 2022: Zhenjiang phase 2 had reached full production (达产), taking the site to ~16 GWh/yr online; phase 3 (~8 GWh) reported as due to begin ramp-up by year-end, for a planned Zhenjiang total of 24 GWh.
Dec 2023: Farasis stated the Zhenjiang factory (three phases, ternary soft-pack/pouch power-battery lines) had completed ramp-up across all phases, i.e. full ~24 GWh/yr online.

Farasis Energy signs investment agreement with Wuhu Sanshan Economic Development Zone (Anhui) to build a 24 GWh/yr new-energy battery base in two phases; phase 1 = 12 GWh, construction expected to start Oct 2021. This is the announced full target, not operational capacity.

Groundbreaking / start of construction of the 24 GWh Wuhu project (reported Jan 2023, delayed from the original Oct 2021 plan). Phase 1 = 12 GWh; per the project plan, completion targeted ~Sep 2023 with trial/formal production late 2023. This 12 GWh is a planned phase-1 target under construction; no source confirms it actually reached operational output.

July 2021 investment/cooperation agreement signed between Changchun city, China FAW and BYD; JV FAW-FinDreams established 15 Jan 2022; construction groundbreaking 26 Feb 2022. Single Changchun power-battery base planned at 45 GWh total across three 15 GWh phases; phase 1 (15 GWh) under construction. Blade battery (LFP). Nothing yet online.
First blade battery pack rolled off the phase-1 line on 21 July 2023 - trial/first output during commissioning, not yet full-rate nameplate. Phase 1 nameplate is 15 GWh.

Phase 1 (15 GWh) officially entered production on 2 Feb 2024; serial/mass production and customer supply from around April 2024 (initial output for FAW Hongqi EV models). This is the only phase actually online.

Full site nameplate target is 45 GWh (3 x 15 GWh phases). As of May 2026 only phase 1 (15 GWh) is operational; phase 2 (planned for 2nd-generation blade battery) was originally targeted around end-2026 but had no firm construction timeline; phase 3 unscheduled. The 45 GWh figure is a plan, NOT online capacity.

Phase 1 (600 mu, 15 GWh, part of 16-line 30 GWh site) production line commissioned (通线) on 16 July 2022; 8 lines reported running by Dec 2022. Site total investment ~10bn yuan, Jinan High-tech Zone LinKong/Airport Economy sub-zone; blade LFP cells.
Phase 2 (550 mu, 15 GWh) production line commissioned February 2023, taking the site to its full 16-line, 30 GWh/yr nameplate. Confirmed by Jinan High-tech Zone government project review.

Jinan government confirms the FinDreams (BYD) Jinan base operating at 30 GWh/yr annual capacity, now producing 2nd-generation flash-charging blade cells. No expansion beyond 30 GWh reported at this site.
Kengzi (Shenzhen) fully automated 8 GWh cell production line completed - the base's first automated line.

BYD Lithium Battery Co. (Kengzi base) opened its total 16 GWh cell capacity to external customers. NB: some trackers describe BYD's Shenzhen+Huizhou power-battery capacity as a combined 16 GWh (10 GWh LFP + 6 GWh NMC), so this figure may bundle small nearby Huizhou lines.

50 GWh of new second-generation Blade battery lines being added at the Kengzi/Pingshan base for high-end Yangwang/Fangchengbao models. As of May 2026 still described as under expansion ('扩建阶段'), not yet fully online - basis planned/under-construction, not confirmed operational.
BYD signs a 30 GWh power-battery base in Xi'an High-Tech Zone (Caotang), CNY12bn; signing ceremony 9 Sept 2018. Target nameplate, not yet built.
Phase 1: 10 GWh ternary-lithium (NMC) cell line at the Caotang factory enters production (external supply and energy-storage cells); construction began 2018.

Separate new-type power battery project announced in Xi'an High-Tech Zone: 12 GWh, CNY7bn, ~1,000 mu (cells and packs). Same metro, distinct plot; operational date/status unconfirmed - not counted as online.
The 30 GWh power-battery base in Xi'an High-Tech Zone (Caotang) reported at full production. Most recent dated operational cumulative nameplate for the core site.
Phase 1 first production lines opened June 2022 — 15 GWh/yr of DM-i blade (LFP) power cells; Phase 1 investment RMB 7bn. This is the first capacity online at the Shengzhou site.
Phase 2 project public notice (July 2025): ~RMB 6bn, 15 GWh/yr power batteries, targeted to complete line commissioning ('通线投产') in 2025. Future capacity at notice date, not yet online.

Joint line-commissioning ('联合通线') ceremony for Phase 2 (15 GWh/yr power cells) and Phase 3 (15 GWh/yr energy-storage cells) held 30 Dec 2025, bringing the site's nameplate to 45 GWh/yr across three phases (still ramping to full output at report time). Total project investment >RMB 24bn (P1 7 + P2 6 + P3 5, some sources ~13.5bn earlier).
Groundbreaking / construction start of the Bishan base, billed as the world's first blade-battery plant (broke ground Feb 2019, phase 1 built in ~1 year).
Phase 1 (8 lithium-ion cell lines) in production; ~10bn yuan investment; 20 GWh/yr nameplate reached (blade battery mass production). OFweek (Dec 2020) confirms 20 GWh reached, next target 35 GWh.
Phase 2 (6 additional lines, +15 GWh) completed and put into production March 2022; Bishan base reaches 35 GWh/yr scaled production capacity.
Land use for the 20 GWh phase-3 power-battery expansion approved (Dec 2022); planned to lift the Bishan base to 55 GWh/yr.

Bishan government confirms new 13.5bn yuan / 20 GWh phase-3 expansion; on completion Bishan base output value ~36bn yuan and capacity 55 GWh/yr. As of this July 2023 disclosure the expansion was still in planning, with no confirmed completion/online date published.

Phase 1 announced: BYD to invest ~RMB 8bn for a 15 GWh/yr power-battery plant in Fuzhou Hi-Tech Zone, Jiangxi. Investment agreement signed at the Jiangxi-GBA cooperation conference (17 Dec 2020); project company 'Fuzhou FinDreams Battery Co.' established 31 Dec 2021. Announcement stated a targeted completion/production date of ~May 2022 and a reserved Phase 2 of a further +15 GWh subject to market demand. This 15 GWh is an announced nameplate target, NOT confirmed as commissioned/online.

As of Oct 2023, Fuzhou municipal government's NEV/parts industry-chain action plan still lists the FinDreams battery project as one to be 'advanced/built out' and to attract upstream battery-material suppliers - i.e. the site was still in the construction/build-up phase with no published operational GWh figure. No dated source confirms any capacity actually online at this site.
Ford announces $3.5bn wholly-owned LFP battery plant in Marshall, MI; ~35 GWh/yr initial target, production slated for 2026 (CATL tech licence).
Ford scales back the plant ~43%, from ~35 GWh/yr to ~20 GWh/yr (jobs cut from 2,500 to 1,700), citing slower EV demand; 2026 start retained.
Plant commissioned: first full LFP prismatic cells produced (slurry to formation/aging/inspection) in June 2026; ~20 GWh/yr nameplate. First US-made mainstream automotive LFP cells.

Feb 2023 non-binding MoU: Ford, LG Energy Solution and Koc Holding to form a JV for a battery cell plant, committing to at least 25 GWh/yr annual capacity (expandable up to 45 GWh/yr), groundbreaking targeted for 2023 and production start in 2026. Project was cancelled/scrapped in Nov 2023 (Koc revoked the pact citing slowing EV uptake) and never built.

Trial production began; official opening event for Form Factory 1 (~520,000-550,000 sq ft) on 12 Sep 2024. Iron-air cell production line commissioned but no GWh nameplate published (online but unquantified).
Commercial production launched in 2025; first commercial deliveries begun (Minnesota pilot). No sourced operational GWh figure for capacity online - remains unquantified in GWh.
Project RAPID first high-volume manufacturing line targeted at up to 20 GWh/yr by 2027 (backed by DOE $150M award announced 20 Sep 2024). Future target, not online.
Full build-out target of 500 MW / ~50 GWh per year by 2028 at ~850,000 sq ft (scaling toward ~1m sq ft). Future target, not online.
Board sanctions (FID) Giga Arctic construction: 29 GWh/yr nameplate, 8 production lines + battery test centre, ~USD 1.7bn capex, production expected H1 2024. Target only.
HENT AS appointed as main construction contractor; construction of the 29 GWh factory commences, production still expected 2024.
EU Innovation Fund awards EUR 100m grant; FREYR states Giga Arctic (29 GWh) proceeding. Still a target; nothing operational.

Q3 2023 results: FREYR elects to MINIMISE Giga Arctic spending in 2024; building to be completed only as a shell ready for 'hot start'; production slips (pending EU/Norway policy vs US IRA). 29 GWh target retained but paused; 0 GWh operational.

29 Aug 2024: FREYR tells staff battery cell production at Mo i Rana is put on hold with major layoffs (China overcapacity / low prices). No Giga Arctic production line was ever commissioned - 0 GWh ever reached operation at this site.
Project announced: Ganfeng Lithium to build annual 10 GWh new-type lithium battery & energy-storage HQ base in Machong, Dongguan; total investment 5bn yuan.
Groundbreaking / construction start of the 10 GWh new-type lithium battery & ESS HQ project in Dongguan (nothing yet online).
Dongguan base officially put into operation on 25 Feb 2026 (投产启用 / 'officially commences operations'); 10 GWh new-type ESS lithium battery capacity, full production ramping through 2026.

Phase I: 2 GWh soft-pack (pouch) LFP production line put into operation (May 2020); the 5 GWh Phase II construction started at the same time. Reported on Ganfeng LiEnergy company development timeline.

Phase II of the Xinyu new-type lithium battery plant commissioned 22 January 2022, taking the site to ~10 GWh/yr annual nameplate on ~330,000 sqm. Reported breakdown: up to 2 GWh/yr solid-state cells + up to 7 GWh/yr prismatic/pouch LFP cells.

Announced expansion target. Aug 2021 Ganfeng disclosed an 84bn-yuan plan including a Xinyu new-type battery project (initially 5 GWh, raised to 10 GWh by the Aug 2022 board resolution); Phase I + Phase II at Xinyu were framed as reaching ~15 GWh/yr combined, with the expansion targeted for ~Oct 2023. NOT confirmed as fully online.
Project signed/settled in Chongqing Liangjiang New Area: 5.4bn yuan, announced 10 GWh/yr battery capacity (initial announcement).

Groundbreaking 30 Jul 2022. Planned full nameplate stated by company as 20 GWh cell + 10 GWh pack (CnEVPost/electrive cite 10 GWh cell + 10 GWh pack - conflict). Aim: China's largest solid-state battery base.
Battery assembly / equipment workshop entered trial operation (21 Feb 2024) per Chongqing municipal government notice. No cell-capacity figure stated.

In trial-operation ramp by Aug 2024; ~6-7 GWh cell capacity expected for 2024; line output 1 module/min, 1 pack/4 min; >1,000 solid-state cells delivered. Same source notes a near-3-month full production halt in autumn 2024 (low utilisation). Recorded 6.5 as midpoint of stated 6-7 GWh.

Company reiterates Chongqing base as full solid-state 'lithium resource-electrolyte-cell' chain with 20 GWh planned nameplate; further cell-line expansion signalled (reports of an additional ~2bn yuan for 4 new cell lines). Target, not online.

MoU signed at WEF Davos (Jan 2024) to set up a 12.5 GWh Li-ion/Na-ion cell manufacturing gigafactory in Telangana; Phase 1 = 2.5 GWh cell assembly line, expanding to ~10 GWh in Phase 2, over 5 years, ~Rs 8,000 crore (~USD 960m). Announced target only — not operational.

Announced 8 Sep 2023 by Gov. Pritzker and Gotion: $2bn conversion of a former Kmart distribution centre in Manteno, IL, targeting 40 GWh/yr of lithium-ion battery CELLS plus 10 GWh/yr of packs, ramping to full nameplate by end of 2034.

Site operational for PACK ASSEMBLY ONLY as of Nov 2025: five lines running (ESS assembly began spring 2025, EV pack assembly from Sep 2025), but packs are assembled from cells imported from Gotion's China plants. In-house LFP CELL manufacturing had NOT yet started; Gotion said it would begin making its own cells 'early next year' (early 2026). Cell capacity actually online at this site = 0 GWh.
Company target: ramp to full nameplate of 40 GWh/yr cells (plus 10 GWh/yr packs) by end of 2034.

Gotion subsidiary Hefei Gotion Jitaimei (国轩极泰) signed a small-power battery cell project with Lujiang High-tech Zone on 11-12 Aug 2025 - Gotion's declared entry into small-power (light EV / two-wheeler / power-tool) cells and its 'third growth pole'. This is the only cell-manufacturing activity sited at Lujiang, and it is an announced/signed project only: no annual GWh capacity was disclosed, and it was neither under construction nor operational at the time of signing.

Nanjing Gotion established in Liuhe Economic Development Zone; first power-battery line, ~2 GWh/yr (RMB1.5bn); signed, built and operational within the year. Source also cites 'initial single workshop, 1 GWh' — conservative ~1-2 GWh.

June 2021: after Volkswagen took a stake, Gotion launched its first direct-investment project in Nanjing — the 'New Energy Intelligent Manufacturing Base', total investment RMB10bn, planned 20 GWh/yr. Construction started Oct 2021.

End-May 2022: first 7 GWh/yr line of the New Energy Intelligent Manufacturing Base (Liuhe District) inaugurated, lifting total Nanjing Gotion capacity to 30 GWh nameplate. Base reached full production by Dec 2022 at ~28 GWh actual.

Global Supply Base in Longpao New City (construction started Dec 2023) formally operational Sept 2024; cumulative Liuhe/Nanjing investment reported >RMB10bn with total capacity approaching ~50 GWh/yr, making Nanjing Gotion's largest global base.
As of Oct 2025 (Nanjing Gotion's 10th anniversary), cumulative Liuhe investment >RMB10bn and total capacity 'near 50 GWh', Gotion's largest production base worldwide.

New 20 GWh/yr new-type lithium-ion intelligent-manufacturing base in Liuhe Economic Development Zone: board-approved Aug 2025, total investment up to RMB4bn, groundbreaking Oct 2025, build period up to 24 months. Not yet in production.
With the new 20 GWh base, the Nanjing hub is targeted to reach ~50 GWh and, on full completion around 2027, to exceed 70 GWh/yr total capacity.

MOU signed between Gotion InoBat Batteries (GIB) and the Slovak government for a gigafactory at Šurany: Phase 1 of 20 GWh, expandable to a total of up to 60 GWh; initial commercial operations targeted for 2026. Nothing built yet.

Slovak government signed the binding Investment Agreement with GIB on 20 June 2024 (JV: Gotion 80%, InoBat 20%; ~EUR 1.2bn). Phase 1 committed at 20 GWh with commercial operations date of 2026, total planned capacity up to 60 GWh; construction planned for end 2024. Still no capacity online.

Construction officially started 28 October 2025 (Šurany, ~65 ha). Phase 1 designed for 20 GWh; pilot/trial production scheduled for September 2026 and serial/mass production for 2027. As of the source date nothing is yet operational — site is under construction.

2024-06-06: investment agreement signed in Rabat (PM Akhannouch). Phase 1 = 20 GWh/yr lithium-ion cell + pack (plus cathode/anode and ESS), initial investment ~USD 1.3bn (MAD 12.8bn); first production targeted Q3 2026. Ultimate site nameplate 100 GWh/yr over five phases, total ~USD 6.5-6.8bn. Nothing online at this date - pure announcement.

2026-05-09: Kenitra plant start of production refined to August 2026 (per BOCOM International note, 6 May 2026). Phase 1 still 20 GWh/yr. Plant NOT yet operational - in advanced preparation, with production-worker and support hiring campaigns underway at the Atlantic Free Zone site. No source confirms any GWh actually in production as of this date.

Company board announcement (19 Nov 2024): Great Power (Guangzhou Great Power Energy / Penghui 鹏辉能源) to build a 10 GWh energy-storage battery-CELL and storage-system manufacturing plant plus a shared-storage R&D base in Guangde, Anhui. Total investment CNY 5bn (~USD 690m). Project split into two phases; phase 2 timing 'per investment plan'. Full-site cell target = 10 GWh/yr.

Phase 1 = 5 GWh/yr of energy-storage cells (plus a 400 MWh shared-storage station), planned to be completed and enter production in September 2025. Confirmed by the Guangde municipal EIA acceptance notice for 'Anhui Great Power Energy Technology 5 GWh/yr storage cell + storage system + 400 MWh shared-storage station project (Phase 1)'. No independently dated commissioning/first-cell-off-line notice found as of research date, so recorded as planned, not confirmed operational.

Great Power (300438.SZ, announcement 2024-033) board approves a project in Chahar Hi-tech Development Zone, Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia comprising a 10 GWh/yr energy storage cell + system integration line and a 1 GWh/yr semi-solid-state cell line; total investment RMB 2.3bn (RMB 1.8bn fixed assets for the 10 GWh ESS project, RMB 0.5bn for the 1 GWh semi-solid project). Nothing online yet — announced targets only.

The 10 GWh/yr energy storage cell project in Ulanqab enters trial production in October 2025 (having broken ground ~September 2024 and targeted operation October 2025). This is the first capacity actually in production at the site; the 1 GWh semi-solid-state line is not yet online.

1 GWh/yr semi-solid-state cell line scheduled to break ground May 2025 and start production July 2026, which would bring the site to 11 GWh/yr nameplate. Future/planned per the 2024 announcement — not confirmed online.

Groundbreaking on 10 Jan 2022 of the Great Power (Penghui Energy) Liuzhou Smart Energy Storage and Power Battery Manufacturing Base in Liuzhou North Ecological New District, Guangxi. Total planned capacity 20 GWh/yr; total investment ~RMB 12bn. This is the announced full-site target, not capacity online.

Phase 1 (and initial phase-2 lines), 4 production lines totalling 5.5 GWh/yr, completed and in full production, making household- and utility-storage cells. Some 2021 company/analyst reports describe this 5.5 GWh as scheduled to come online at end-2021; confirmed in full production by 2022.

Around 15 May 2023 an additional ~5 GWh/yr (4 production lines) came online at the Liuzhou base, taking the industrial park to a full annual production capacity of 10.5 GWh/yr (reported by BJX/Beijixing energy-storage news, citing local sources).

Base broke ground in Chengyang District, Qingdao, Sept 2023. Announced full plan: 36 GWh across three 12 GWh phases (314Ah LFP large ESS cells), ~13bn yuan, ~1,000 mu. Nothing online yet at this date - this is the announced full-site target, not installed capacity.

Phase 1 (12 GWh, 275 mu, three LFP cell lines A/B/C + one solid-state line) commissioned in 2025: feed/trial production from 6 Jun 2025, 100Ah line into production end-Jul, 314Ah LFP line reached full production (满产) by end-Aug; reported running at full capacity ('super factory at full production') on 10 Sep 2025. Only Phase 1 (12 GWh) is online; Phases 2-3 not yet built.
Construction of Greater Bay/Juwan Nansha HQ and manufacturing base started (May 2022); full planned capacity 8 GWh/yr, total investment ~RMB4bn (40亿元), ~189,000 m2 site.
Groundbreaking / main-structure start of the Nansha energy-storage & cell production base on 8 Feb 2023; designed capacity 8 GWh/yr (includes cell production, safety-test and PACK workshops).
Factory formally put into production 30 Oct 2023 (world's first XFC ultra-fast-charge power-cell factory). Phase-1 cell capacity 4 GWh/yr online (一期产能4GWh, 投资约25亿元); '目前已投入使用4GWh'.
Full build-out target for the Nansha site is 8 GWh/yr (remaining ~4 GWh phase-2). No dated source confirms this second phase was commissioned as of mid-2026.

Project signed 20 Nov 2025 for the Suining Economic & Technological Development Zone (Sichuan): 20 GWh/yr sodium-ion cell capacity (+10 GWh/yr pack), total investment ~CNY6.0-6.1bn on ~500 mu, phased. Phase 1 = 10 GWh/yr cells + 5 GWh/yr pack on ~280 mu. Full completion/production targeted before April 2027. Nothing online yet.

CNY200m A-round (sole investor Suining Industrial Investment) announced ~27 Apr 2026, earmarked to build an 8 GWh/yr intelligent production line at the Suining base (40160 large-cylindrical sodium-ion cells), matching the Guangde base process. Construction-financing stage; still pre-operational (no capacity online).

Hefei Gotion signs agreement with Hefei Xinzhan Hi-Tech Zone management committee to build a 20 GWh/yr power-battery base dedicated to Volkswagen unified cells (phase 1 of 10 GWh planned within ~16-18 months); ~CNY 6.7bn investment.

Gotion states the Hefei Xinzhan VW standard-cell project (20 GWh; 10 GWh NMC + 10 GWh LFP) is expected to enter production in Q4 2023 to supply C-samples to VW; main workshop/buildings near complete but not yet in mass production.

Fundraising project renamed from 'Annual 20 GWh VW standard-cell project' to 'VW standard-cell line project' and revised to 28 GWh/yr (12 GWh NMC + 16 GWh LFP) plus PACK, at the Hefei Xinzhan site - a future/planned expansion, not yet online.

Mass production and first delivery of VW unified cells begins; handover ceremony held 20 Nov 2025 at the Hefei Xinzhan UC plant (attended by VW CTO Thomas Schmall, PowerCo CEO Frank Blome, Gotion chairman Li Zhen). Plant annual production capacity stated as 20 GWh; LFP and other chemistries; supply to VW 2026-2032.

First 100-million-cell/yr 18650 lithium line commissioned (H1 2016) beside the PV park on Hengdian ring road; base lithium capacity ~1 GWh (the 'original 1 GWh' cited in later IR). GWh is IR-stated, not a precise cell-level disclosure.
148-million-cell high-performance lithium project commissioned Aug 2021; total lithium capacity rose from ~1 GWh to 2.5 GWh.
6 GWh high-performance lithium battery project announced Jan 2022 (~CNY 1.833bn, Dongci High-Tech Industrial Park, Hengdian); expected on-line Q4 2022, targeting ~7 GWh total base capacity.
Operational lithium-cell capacity 2.5 GWh as of 31 Dec 2022 (18650/21700 cylindrical); the 6 GWh project still ramping/in construction at year-end.
6 GWh Dongci High-Tech Park project came into production during 2023; total operational lithium-cell capacity 7 GWh (reported as 8 lines across three workshops).
Lithium-cell capacity held at 7 GWh at end-2024 (18650/21700 ternary cylindrical), per 2024 annual report.
Company states it now has 8 GWh/yr lithium-cell capacity (18650/21700 ternary cylindrical), per 2025 half-year report.
Phase 1 'M1' smart factory brought into production - 5 lithium-battery lines, 15 GWh/yr (LFP energy-storage cells). First cells rolled off 28 May 2022; handover/production announced 29 May 2022.

Phase 2 (二期, Tongxiang High-Tech Zone) - 30 GWh/yr, 8 production lines, ~RMB 4bn, LFP ESS cells - reached production in May 2023, taking the Xiamen base to ~45 GWh/yr. Groundbreaking was June 2022; the phase-2 project details are described in this Xiamen government source.

Phase 1 (10 GWh/yr) reached commercial production in April 2024; plant inaugurated by President Joko Widodo on 3 July 2024 as Southeast Asia's first EV battery cell plant. Phase 1 investment ~US$1.1bn.
Phase 2 (adds 20 GWh/yr; construction began January 2024, ~US$2bn) began commercial operation in March 2025, raising total site nameplate capacity to 30 GWh/yr.

Honda announces a stand-alone EV battery plant in Alliston, Ontario, with 36 GWh/yr capacity once fully operational; EV/battery production targeted for 2028. Part of a ~CAD$15bn (~USD$11bn) Ontario EV value-chain plan (separate from the LG Energy Solution JV in Ohio).

Honda announces an approximate two-year postponement of the entire Canadian value-chain project (incl. the 36 GWh Alliston battery plant), citing the EV-market slowdown and US tariff uncertainty. Capacity target unchanged but start pushed ~2 years; nothing built.

Honda indefinitely suspends the $15bn Ontario EV complex, including the Alliston battery plant, as it pivots to hybrids. The 36 GWh plant was never constructed; no cell capacity ever came online at this site.
InoBat announces plan (MoU with Serbia) to build an EV battery factory of up to 32 GWh/yr in Serbia; site not yet chosen.

InoBat signs MoU with Serbia's Ministry of Finance and the Municipality of Cuprija; Cuprija selected for 'Project Lion'. Phase 1 of 4 GWh/yr targeted to open in 2025; full nameplate up to 32 GWh/yr across multiple phases.

EUR 419m Serbian government incentives package confirmed; construction of the up-to-32 GWh/yr facility stated to begin in 2025, first phase 4 GWh. 32 GWh is the ultimate multi-phase nameplate, no dated completion year given.

IBC MoU with Government of Karnataka (Aug 2023): build a lithium-ion (NMC prismatic) cell gigafactory near Bengaluru (Devanahalli), starting with a 2 GWh Phase 1 facility targeted for 2025 (a 'copy exact' of its Korean plant). Reported at the Jan 2024 USD 35M raise. Target, not yet online.
Full-build target of 10 GWh/yr by 2028 at the same Bengaluru site under the Karnataka MoU; total investment ~INR 8,000 crore (~USD 1bn), ~100 acres at Devanahalli. Announced target, not online.

Groundbreaking of the Phase 1 unit (~Jan 2025), in a JV with Mahanagar Gas Ltd; ~INR 390 crore investment, >1 GWh initial annual production line within the 2 GWh Phase 1, with production expected within ~9 months (i.e. late 2025).
