Construction milestone - capacity not yet confirmed operational. (Note: some sources instead cite a Sept 2024 Phase 1 groundbreaking - see notes.)

Italvolt announces 45 GWh/yr cell gigafactory on the former Olivetti site at Scarmagno (Piedmont), with a stated potential later expansion to 70 GWh/yr; production targeted for 2024. Never reached operation.
Phase 1 sodium-ion cell line (4.5 GWh/yr) put into operation at the end of March 2023 at the Gaoyou site.
Phase 2 (+5.5 GWh/yr, to reach ~10 GWh total) financed via a targeted share issue; announced/planned, not yet built.
Company confirms Phase 1 4.5 GWh remains the only line in production, at low utilisation; Phase 2 still not online.
Original Changshu Zenergy base ('software-defined' plant, ~25 GWh design capacity) begins operations 9 May 2023 — company's first cell base.

At its Hong Kong IPO (listed 14 Apr 2025) Zenergy reports total designed production capacity of 25.5 GWh (company-wide), demand already exceeding it; Yinhe/Galaxy B-Zone base under construction, phase 1 due Q4 2025.

Changshu Yinhe/Galaxy (银河) B-Zone 25 GWh automotive lithium battery base (CNY 10bn, ~741 mu) tops out 7 Jun 2025; phase 1 (10 GWh) targeted Q4 2025, phase 2 (15 GWh) by end-2026, lifting company-wide total to 50.5 GWh. Separate physical base from the original Changshu base.

Company-wide capacity reached 35.5 GWh as of May 2026 (up 39.2% from 25.5 GWh), reflecting Galaxy B-Zone phase 1 (~10 GWh) coming online. Company guides to 70 GWh by end-2026 (conflicts with the 50.5 GWh buildout figure) and ~120 GWh within 2-3 years.

Feb 2024 Odisha MoU (Rs 40,000 cr integrated EV + battery complex, Cuttack/Paradip): phase-1 target of 10 GWh cell + battery manufacturing by 2026, within a planned 50 GWh facility. Technology tie-up sought, no equity partner. Not operational.
Same Feb 2024 Odisha plan: phase-2 expansion to 50 GWh total, targeted ~2028-2030. Announced target only.

Dec 2024: JSW in talks with LG Energy Solution for a jointly owned 10 GWh cell/battery gigafactory in India (>$1.5bn; LGES supplying technology/equipment), production targeted by end-2026. Talks stage, not operational; location not confirmed.

June 2026: JSW reported to have 'finalised' a 30 GWh Li-ion CELL plant with a JV partner, >$1.3bn, in two phases (phase 1 ~10 GWh ~$700-750m; phase 2 +20 GWh ~$600m). Location NOT decided (Southeast Asia cited as an option); in the interim JSW imports cells from China. Announced/planned, not under construction at a confirmed site.

Groundbreaking ceremony (11 Sep 2023) at Dongbusan E-PARK industrial complex, Gijang-gun, Busan. Announced full nameplate ~16.2 GWh: 300 million cells/yr = 200M 21700 cells (3.7 GWh) + 100M 4695 cells (~12.5 GWh). ~KRW 610bn investment; completion planned Dec 2024; mass production from 2025.

Phased target reaffirmed: 21700 line 3.7 GWh (mass production targeted Jan 2025) + 4695 line 12.6 GWh (mass production targeted June 2025), ~16.3 GWh combined nameplate. Nothing yet online; construction ongoing (reported ~70% complete, ~KRW 577bn spent, late 2024) with completion slipping from Dec 2024.

Phase 1 (21700 line, 3.7 GWh nameplate) began limited production. First cell shipment to Nanotech Energy on 30 Jan 2025 (~KRW 4.8bn); construction completion and 21700 mass production slipped to ~Apr/May 2025. Actual output volumes were small; the 4695 phase (12.6 GWh) was NOT commissioned. 3.7 GWh is the phase-1 line nameplate, not verified realised throughput.

Build-out stalled. Company failed to reach full mass production; the Gijang site entered forced auction over unpaid construction costs and Kumyang faced KOSPI delisting (second consecutive disclaimer of audit opinion). The 4695 (12.6 GWh) phase never came online; no verified operational capacity at full nameplate.

Groundbreaking (28 Feb 2023) for the LG Energy Solution / Honda JV plant; ~40 GWh/yr nameplate targeted, ~US$3.5-4.4bn invested, originally pouch-type Li-ion for Honda EVs, mass production planned by end of 2025. Not yet online.

Mass production of ESS Li-ion battery cells began 1 July 2026 at the completed Jeffersonville plant (~40 GWh/yr nameplate). Strategy pivoted from EV to ESS; cells supplied to LG Energy Solution Vertech. Figure is full nameplate at start of mass production; real online output ramps from initial lines.

Phase 1 (~16 GWh) production line commissioned / trial-mass production, June 2022; ~3bn yuan output value that year. (Note: some secondary sources date line commissioning to June 2021 - treated as a conflicting/erroneous date.)
Phase 3 signed 3 Mar 2023: new 45 GWh cell + module lines (16 cell lines), ~11bn yuan investment, taking the Jiashan site's planned full-ramp capacity to 77 GWh.

Groundbreaking of the combined Phase 2+3 expansion (stated as a 63 GWh lithium-ion battery + research institute project), total investment >13.5bn yuan, production expected from H2 2024; full-ramp site total quoted as 79 GWh (16 existing + 63 added).
Phase 2 (16 GWh) construction completed ~Jan 2024, bringing commissioned capacity at the Jiashan site to ~32 GWh (Phase 1 + Phase 2); Phase 3 45 GWh still under construction.
Initial announcement: $1.4bn cylindrical EV cell plant in Queen Creek, Arizona, 11 GWh nameplate.
Project rescoped to a $5.5bn complex: 27 GWh cylindrical EV plant + 16 GWh LFP ESS plant = 43 GWh combined, ground-break planned 2023.
Capacity target raised to 53 GWh (36 GWh cylindrical EV + 17 GWh LFP ESS); cylindrical plant completion targeted 2025, ESS 2026.

As of Mar 2025 the cylindrical plant was ~50% built and targeting start of 46mm cell mass production in spring 2026; the LFP ESS plant reported paused/on hold. 53 GWh remains the planned full-nameplate complex total.
Reported operating capacity ~10 GWh/yr in mid-2021 (CONFLICT: a second figure of ~17 GWh/yr also cited; both trace only to the weak Grokipedia page — low confidence, conservative value taken)
'Current' Ochang capacity of 21 GWh/yr per S&P Global (part of LGES plan to more than double company-wide capacity to 520 GWh/yr by 2025)

4680 (46-series) cylindrical 'mother line', ~9 GWh/yr (KRW 580bn), began series production at Ochang in Aug 2024 (announced June 2022 as part of a KRW 730bn / +13 GWh cylindrical expansion: 2170 +4 GWh, 4680 +9 GWh)

Target capacity of 33 GWh/yr for Ochang by 2025 (S&P Global, 2022); a related June 2022 expansion announcement framed the post-expansion figure as ~35 GWh/yr — target never confirmed as fully online in a dated source
Separate domestic LFP-for-ESS line planned to start commercial production at Ochang in 2027, initially ~1 GWh/yr

Existing/initial annual capacity of the Wrocaw (Biskupice Podgrne) plant stated as 'over 35 GWh' at the time the EIB EUR480m expansion loan was signed; production had begun H2 2017 and ramped through 2018. This 35 GWh is repeatedly cited as the plant's initial nameplate.

European Commission State aid decision states the new investment programme 'enabled the company to ramp up its battery capacity output to ca. 65 GWh', making it one of the largest Li-ion cell factories in the world. Official/dated figure.

LG Energy Solution / trade press describe Wrocaw as Europe's largest battery plant with annual capacity of approximately 86 GWh as of 2023. NOTE: conflicts with a Dec-2024 LGES source that cites 70 GWh current capacity (see notes); treated as lower confidence.
Announced target to raise Wrocaw annual capacity from 70 GWh to 115 GWh by end-2025 (a separate 'stage IV' framing cites a 100 GWh target). Future/planned, not online.
Fifth production line completed (announced Jan 2018 for Aug 2018 completion, $9.4M), raising NMC EV pouch-cell capacity to ~3 GWh/yr.
Existing NMC EV pouch-cell capacity stated at 5 GWh/yr, the baseline cited when the $1.7bn expansion was announced on 22 Mar 2022.
22 Mar 2022 plan: $1.7bn to expand from 5 GWh to 25 GWh/yr by 2025 (EV-focused). Later revised/superseded by the pivot to LFP ESS cells; not met as originally framed.
New LFP battery-cell plant opened 24 Jun 2025 with 16.5 GWh/yr ESS capacity (two of three lines running), on top of 5 GWh/yr existing NMC EV production, giving a total site capacity of 21.5 GWh/yr.

Q2 2025 earnings call (28 Jul 2025): ESS-line capacity to reach 30 GWh/yr by year-end 2026 (17 GWh by end-2025); combined with retained ~5 GWh NMC-EV production implies ~35 GWh/yr total site nameplate. Target/plan, not yet online.
Announced as Ultium Cells' 3rd US cell plant (GM-LG Energy Solution JV), $2.6bn investment, ~50 GWh/yr at full production; construction begun 2022, opening expected late 2024. Not online.

On announcing sale of GM's JV stake to LG Energy Solution, capacity guidance revised down: ~27 GWh/yr initial. Plant described as nearly complete but not yet producing; year shown is expected initial-production year, not confirmed online.
Same Dec 2024 GM stake-sale guidance: capacity rising to ~36 GWh/yr by 2027. Announced target, not online.
Master plan for the Suzhou 21700 base announced: planned total annual capacity 15 GWh, total investment ~5bn yuan, 530 mu. This is a target, never fully built.

Phase 1 (21700/18650 cylindrical) formally built and into production on 20 July 2017 (groundbreaking 15 April 2016); ~4 GWh built, phase 1&2 investment ~2.1bn yuan. China's first customised 21700 line.
Reached full production in 2018 at 4 GWh/yr annual capacity; ~1bn yuan revenue that year (customers incl. JAC, Changan Oushang, Suzhou Higer).

New-generation cylindrical (21700 all-tab) R&D + production base (phase 2) broke ground 17 Nov 2023 in Suzhou High-Tech Zone: planned 7.3 GWh, ~174 mu, 5 lines, ~2.75bn yuan, planned completion end-2024.

New-generation cylindrical base launched/put into operation via ceremony on 8 July 2025: 7.3 GWh of 21700 all-tab cells across 5 intelligent lines, ~2.75-2.8bn yuan investment. Additive to existing ~4 GWh -> ~11.3 GWh online at the site.
Phase 1 (4 GWh, '40亿瓦时', LFP prismatic power + storage cells) put into production 29 Apr 2019; total investment RMB1.57bn.
Full Qingdao base planned annual capacity of 10 GWh LFP prismatic cells (phase 1 online, phase 2 to follow) - would be Shandong's largest power-battery base at full ramp.

Qingdao base power-battery capacity cited at ~4 GWh (of Lishen group total 8 GWh split Tianjin 4 GWh + Qingdao 4 GWh), ahead of the China FAW / state-owned acquisition announced 25 Sept 2024. No phase-2 commissioning datable between 2019 and 2024.

2025 corporate capacity plan lists Qingdao at 10 GWh (energy storage). Site renamed China Auto New Energy (Qingdao) Battery Technology (中汽新能) following state-owned integration; 工商变更 confirmed 14/18 Jul 2025.
Phase 1 (10 GWh LFP) construction started, October 2020. JV of Gotion High-tech and Liuzhou Dongcheng (East City) Group in Liudong New Area; total site planned at 30 GWh across ~968 mu.
First 5 GWh cell line began supplying cells and packs, October 2021.
Phase 1 10 GWh base put into operation 30 July 2022; reached full 10 GWh production in September 2022 (six months ahead of schedule).
Phase 2 (20 GWh) officially broke ground 27 September 2022, taking full-build target to 30 GWh/yr for the site. Total investment no less than RMB 10bn.
Phase 2 first-stage 5 GWh line put into production, early May 2024 (mass production expected late May/early June 2024), adding to the 10 GWh Phase 1 already online.

Lucas TVS signs licence/services agreement with 24M Technologies to build a SemiSolid lithium-ion CELL gigafactory at Thervoy Kandigai (SIPCOT, Gummidipoondi), Tamil Nadu. Stated ambition: grow the site to 10 GWh in two stages; phase 1 (a smaller first stage, GWh not specified) planned to begin commercial production in H2 2023. This is the announced cell-manufacturing target, not capacity online.

SIPCOT Thervoy Kandigai facility (operated by TVS Indeon, subsidiary of Lucas TVS) began operations in 2024 at ~1 GWh, supplying TVS Motor Company. IMPORTANT SCOPE FLAG: sources describe this as lithium-ion battery PACK production/assembly (packs per day), NOT cell manufacturing. No dated source confirms 24M SemiSolid CELL lines commissioned. Recorded and flagged, not to be read as cell capacity online.
Construction begins (Oct 2019); initial facility planned at 16 GWh/yr (two 8 GWh blocks), with intent to expand to at least 32 GWh.
Northvolt raises $2.75bn equity; announces expansion of the Skellefteå gigafactory's planned annual capacity to 60 GWh/yr (up from ~40 GWh).
First lithium-ion cell assembled at Northvolt Ett on 28 Dec 2021; first production block being commissioned (first-phase nameplate 16 GWh/yr). Actual output negligible at this point.

EIB provides >$1bn as part of $5bn project financing; plan described as expanding annual output to up to 60 GWh/yr, comprising a 42 GWh vertically-integrated cell facility plus cathode and recycling. Target, not online.

On 23 Sept 2024 Northvolt suspends the second cell fab / expansion and cuts 1,600 jobs, refocusing on ramping the existing first fab to its 16 GWh/yr nameplate. Northvolt files Chapter 11 on 21 Nov 2024. Online nameplate remains ~16 GWh (actual production far below).

Lyten completes acquisition of Northvolt Sweden (26 Feb 2026): ~16 GWh/yr operational cell capacity at Northvolt Ett, plus >15 GWh under construction; site infrastructure stated to be scalable beyond 100 GWh.

Megamillion Energy Company (CEO Nechan Naicker) plans a ~0.25 GWh/yr pilot cell plant (described as scaleable) to open in H2 2020 at the Coega SEZ, Eastern Cape. ~USD 35m, privately funded. Not confirmed to have ever gone operational.
2020 announcement target: ramp cell output to ~32 GWh/yr by 2028 (ESS market first, then EV). This is the origin of the 32 GWh/2028 figure in our record.

Feb 2025: Megamillion announces JV with Dr Henry Mao (co-founder of Tianjin Lishen) to build 'Giga-Africa 1', beginning at 1 GWh/yr, dry cells initially produced in China with electrolyte-filling and post-processing in SA, scaling to 32 GWh/yr 'on completion' (no firm date given). Still an announcement — no confirmed groundbreaking or construction.
Battery MODULE assembly began Oct 2024 using imported LG cells (Poland). No on-site cell manufacturing yet, so zero cell capacity online at this site.
On-site LFP battery CELL mass production officially began 18 Nov 2025 after commissioning; plant nameplate design capacity 49.5 GWh/yr (up from original 45 GWh plan).
Northvolt announces 'Northvolt Drei' third gigafactory in Heide: 60 GWh/yr nameplate planned, first cell production targeted for late 2025. Nothing built.
Groundbreaking / start of construction (25 March 2024). 60 GWh/yr nameplate reaffirmed; production start pushed to 2026, full capacity targeted by 2029. Site-preparation/piling only — 0 GWh online.
Northvolt AB bankrupt (US Chapter 11 21 Nov 2024; Sweden 12 Mar 2025). Heide construction stalled at prepared-site stage; no cell production line commissioned — 0 GWh operational.

US firm Lyten (buyer of the site, deal approved Sep 2025) plans a scaled-back, phased factory of roughly 15 GWh initial capacity and ~1,000 jobs. First partial construction permit (Federal Immission Control Act) issued April 2026; still no cells produced — 0 GWh online.
Announced 28 Sep 2023: phase 1 of 30 GWh/yr cell capacity, first battery cells targeted for 2026. Construction of first 30 GWh phase due to start before end of 2023.
Announced 28 Sep 2023: phase 2 doubles output to full nameplate of 60 GWh/yr, full capacity targeted for 2028.

Project halted (site prep/foundation work suspended spring 2025 after parent bankruptcy) and formally cancelled by Quebec in September 2025 after no binding buyer met the 1 Sep 2025 deadline. No cell capacity was ever commissioned; actual online capacity = 0 GWh/yr.
Phase 1a completed March 2024 with 1.4 GWh of installed cell capacity (equipment/manufacturing readiness; commercial cell production only began mid-2025).
Ola Cell commissioned 2.5 GWh of installed capacity by Q2 FY26, described as India's first gigawatt-scale operational cell facility; Bharat 4680 NMC cells entering customer vehicles.

Terminal Phase-1 target of ~5.9 GWh gross (~5 GWh net); ramp-up completion targeted by September 2026 with >2 GWh of cells expected produced by then. Slipped from an earlier 'by March 2026' target stated in the Nov 2025 Q2 FY26 release.
Announced May 2026: plan to expand cell capacity to 20 GWh by H2 FY27, funded at the cell-entity level. Explicitly deferred/contingent on demand scaling up (earlier IPO-era 20 GWh plan pushed back).
ONE announces $1.6bn ONE Circle cell factory in Van Buren Township, Michigan; 20 GWh/yr full nameplate targeted at full ramp (by end of 2027). No capacity online yet.

10 MWh (0.01 GWh/yr) LFP pilot line begins production at ONE Circle - the first and only confirmed operational cell capacity at the site. Used to validate cell designs and share samples with customers.

Stated target of 20 GWh/yr full nameplate by end of 2027 (~200,000 EV packs/yr). Never realised: ONE suspended EV-battery investment and pivoted to rail/defence/ESS in January 2026 after repeated layoffs; no multi-GWh commercial line was ever confirmed operational.
By mid/Aug 2018 Panasonic's cell production capacity at Giga Nevada had reached ~20 GWh/yr (per Tesla Q2 2018 update), ramping toward the 35 GWh design nameplate.

March 2019: Panasonic announced it had reached its initial 35 GWh/yr nameplate (13 lines installed). DISPUTED - in April 2019 Musk said real output was only ~24 GWh/yr and Panasonic was the constraint. 35 GWh = installed nameplate, not demonstrated output.
14th production line - announced Aug/Sep 2020 with ~$100m investment, raising nameplate ~10% from 35 to ~39 GWh/yr; line came online early 2021.
June 2023 (Nikkei, via Electrek): Panasonic reported plans for a 15th line for 2170 cells to add ~10% capacity within 1-2 years, taking nameplate from ~38-39 to ~42 GWh/yr. TARGET, not yet online.

By 2025 Panasonic/coverage cites the Nevada plant's current annual capacity at ~41 GWh/yr, having delivered >11 billion cells (context: Panasonic opened its second US plant in Kansas, ~32 GWh, July 2025).
Groundbreaking on 2 Nov 2022; >$4bn investment, planned ~30 GWh/yr of 2170 cylindrical cells, mass production originally targeted by March 2025 and full operation by 2027.

Mass production of 2170 cylindrical Li-ion cells began 14 Jul 2025 (grand opening). Panasonic states the site is 'aiming for' ~32 GWh/yr annual nameplate; this is installed nameplate now ramping, not achieved output. Full-production ramp has been slowed vs the original 2027 target (no new full-capacity date given).

Announced target: ~16 GWh/yr at Oizumi (Gunma) alone by end of 2030. Plant is a Subaru–Panasonic Energy JV to make next-gen cylindrical Li-ion cells for Subaru EVs. Two buildings; building 1 operational FY2028, building 2 FY2029; mass production from fiscal 2028.

Panasonic announced (28 Feb 2022) it would build two new 4680 cylindrical-cell production lines at the Wakayama Factory. Capacity ~10 GWh/yr per Nikkei estimate (NOT officially confirmed by Panasonic; company disclosed neither capacity nor investment). Mass production originally targeted for FY ending March 2024.

Panasonic Energy said (9 Sept 2024) it had finalised preparations and was 'ready to commence mass production' of 4680 cells at Wakayama, with an opening ceremony held; production to begin only after a final evaluation (~400 staff by Mar 2025). Still not confirmed operational; capacity target unchanged at ~10 GWh/yr (media estimate). Production subsequently delayed past end of March 2026.

Groundbreaking 10 Jan 2022 in Liuzhou Northern Ecological New District; overall planned nameplate 20 GWh, total investment ~6bn yuan (initial phase 1+2 framed as ~4 GWh at announcement). Target, not yet online.
Phase 1 lines commissioned; trial/mass production from ~19 Oct 2022; 5.5 GWh/yr online (per 2022 annual report).
'Phase 3' put into production end-May 2023, lifting the base's annual output capacity to 10.5 GWh/yr (5.5 GWh phase 1 + ~5 GWh increment).

Master-plan signed 28 Mar 2018 for the Suchu Modern Industrial Park base in Chuzhou: 25 GWh/yr across four phases, ~10bn yuan, ~700 mu. Phase 1 billed at 6 GWh (3bn yuan) for Q2 2019; phase 2 at 13 GWh (12 lines) by end-2020; whole project to reach 25 GWh by 2022. (Some later sources cite a 50 GWh ultimate ambition.)

Chuzhou base unveiled 21 Jan 2019 (phase 1 then billed as 5 GWh to start April 2019); phase 1 actually came online during 2019 at ~3.5 GWh/yr per company/Baidu figures. Conservative operational value used given the 3.5 vs 5 vs 6 GWh conflict across sources.

'Golden Brick' (金砖) vehicle-grade EV/ESS cell line phase 1 commissioned (ribbon-cutting) 24 May 2023, adding ~1.6 GWh/yr; phase 2 (4 GWh) signed the same day, for a combined +5.6 GWh planned. Cumulative left null - unclear whether this line sits inside or on top of the phase-1 envelope.
Chuzhou phase 1 rated at 8 GWh/yr, re-filed in Sept 2022 up from the original 6 GWh design; phase 2 (4 GWh) under construction at this point.

New 4 GWh/yr power+ESS cell and pack project (models 15119/17119/21119): groundbreaking 25 Apr 2024, topping-out 10 Oct 2024, total investment 1.83bn yuan; construction finished Sept 2024, commissioning planned for Dec 2024. Kept as target, not confirmed online.

Construction start signal given (17 Mar 2023) in presence of King Felipe VI and PM Pedro Sanchez. Announced annual capacity of 40 GWh/yr, expandable to 60 GWh, with unified-cell production planned to start in 2026. Nothing online — future target.

Revised plan (electrive, 28 Oct 2025): series cell production now scheduled to start July 2027 with two production blocks totalling 20 GWh/yr; preseries/pilot phase Sep-Oct 2026. Site designed for two further blocks up to 40 GWh/yr total. Still under construction — future target, not online.
Groundbreaking on 7 July 2022 (with Chancellor Scholz). PowerCo announced up to 20 GWh/yr initial capacity, expandable to up to 40 GWh/yr if required. Nothing online yet (planned).

Gigafactory commissioned 17 December 2025; first Unified Cells 'made in Europe' produced. Phase-1 nameplate of up to 20 GWh/yr installed, output ramping up gradually through 2026 (real utilisation far below nameplate at commissioning). Expansion to up to 40 GWh/yr remains conditional ('if required'), no committed date.

Announced (VW Group / PowerCo SE): St. Thomas cell gigafactory with up to 90 GWh/yr annual capacity in the final expansion phase, across six production blocks. Groundbreaking planned 2024, production to start 2027, investment up to EUR 4.8bn / CAD 7bn 'until 2030' (used as the final-phase horizon).
Planned first cell production year (reaffirmed on track). No day-one nameplate GWh figure is published for 2027 - only the eventual 'up to 90 GWh' final-phase target exists.

Construction of the first three major buildings began (28 Oct 2025). PowerCo reaffirmed the up-to-90 GWh/yr capacity target and a 2027 production start; still no capacity online and no phased GWh breakdown disclosed.

PPES announces a new BEV prismatic Li-ion production line at Himeji as part of an Aug 2022 production-capability enhancement plan, expanding capacity by approximately 7 GWh/year, targeted to start production in 2024.

PPES starts up the new Himeji production line and begins mass production of a new prismatic Li-ion BEV cell (for Toyota bZ4X, Lexus RZ, Subaru Solterra). This is the line from the Aug 2022 enhancement plan (~7 GWh/year); reports indicate mass production commenced during 2025. No source publishes a cumulative operational total, so the ~7 GWh increment is carried from the 2022 plan.

PPES to begin producing next-generation 'performance' BEV batteries at Himeji from 2026; after that ramp the facility's total capacity is expected to reach approximately 30 GWh/year, described as one of the largest in Japan.
Original Choose France announcement (with President Macron): EUR 5.2bn gigafactory, up to 48 GWh ultimate phased capacity; production originally targeted by end of 2026. Later delayed.
Revised roadmap (post EV-market slowdown): Phase 1 completion in 2028 with initial mass-production capacity of 0.8 GWh/yr; production start pushed from 2026 to 2028.
Planned ramp to 4 GWh/yr (Phase 2 at full capacity) by 2030.
At groundbreaking (10 Feb 2026), ProLogium confirmed initial annual capacity of 0.8 GWh, facility completion 2028.
Groundbreaking roadmap: capacity increased from 2029, reaching 4 GWh/yr by 2030 (Phase 2 full).
Fab 1 full nameplate capacity of 12 GWh/yr targeted by 2032. Site has long-term potential to scale to 48 GWh subject to demand (no committed year).

Groundbreaking at Karawang New Industry City (KNIC), West Java on 29 June 2025; construction of the CATIB cell/module/pack plant begins. Phase 1 nameplate stated as 6.9 GWh/yr, total 15 GWh/yr; first production targeted for end-2026. Nothing online yet at groundbreaking.
Phase 1 nameplate of 6.9 GWh/yr targeted to come online in 2026 (originally end-2026). This is an announced target at groundbreaking, not confirmed production.

Feb 2026 Indonesian trade-press update: CATIB brings production start forward to ~June/July 2026 (from Sept 2026). Plant still under construction / pre-operational; Phase 1 remains 6.9 GWh/yr, total 15 GWh/yr. No dated source confirms cells actually in production as of July 2026.
Full 15 GWh/yr nameplate after Phase 2 expansion (+8.1 GWh/yr), targeted 'by the end of the decade'. Announced target only.

REPT Battero board approves investment in non-wholly-owned subsidiary PT REPT Battero Indonesia (60% REPT via Infinitude International Investment; combined USD 139.5m injection). Phase-1 target of 8 GWh/yr lithium-ion power and energy-storage cell gigafactory announced - REPT's first overseas base.

REPT Battero officially opens / debuts its first overseas manufacturing base (lithium-ion cell + BESS) in Indonesia at ICEE 2026 (Jakarta, 11-13 May 2026). Phase-1 nameplate 8 GWh/yr; TKDN local-content and SNI certifications expected June 2026. Opening marks phase-1 commissioning; real output ramping.

Groundbreaking of Pylontech 10 GWh Li-ion battery R&D + manufacturing base in Feixi Economic Development Zone, Hefei (RMB 5bn). Built in two 5 GWh phases; Phase 1 (5 GWh) construction began Dec 2022. The 10 GWh is the full-buildout target, none online yet.

Phase 1 (5 GWh cell + system-assembly lines) commissioned. Trial production ~June 2023, full production ~Sept 2023 per later provincial/company reporting. Some secondary summaries round Phase 1 completion to 2024; primary reporting supports 2023.

Phase 2 (+5 GWh cell + system-assembly, ~68 mu) groundbreaking 20 Dec 2025 in Feixi; targeted equipment install end-2026 and operational ~end-2026, bringing site to 10 GWh nameplate. A fundraising-project delay was filed Sept 2025. Not online as of July 2026.

Groundbreaking on 26 Feb 2022 of QingTao's solid-state lithium cell industrialisation project in Kunshan Development Zone, Jiangsu. Total investment 5bn yuan (50亿元); design/full nameplate stated as 10 GWh/yr. Nothing online yet at this new project.

Main structure of the Kunshan 10 GWh solid-state cell project topped out (结构封顶) in Aug 2023. Construction milestone only - no cell capacity commissioned/online at this point. Contradicts the existing record's implied 2023 production start.

Phase 1 entered mass production in June 2024. Phase-1 annual nameplate 3.5 GWh/yr (一期 35亿瓦时). Described by Chinese trade press as China's largest / a globally leading solid-state cell mass-production line. This is the first capacity actually online at the site.
Full-production (达产) design target for the project is 10 GWh/yr (100亿瓦时), stated as reachable within roughly 3 years of the 2024 phase-1 start (i.e. ~2027). Not yet online.

Groundbreaking (18 Oct 2022) of the Quzhou smart energy storage battery base in Quzhou Smart Manufacturing New City; announced ~20 GWh/yr, total investment ~6bn yuan, phase 1 ~10 GWh planned. Nothing online yet.
Phase 1 (~11 GWh/yr) ignited and put into production on 19 Jun 2023; 282 mu site, phase-1 investment >3bn yuan. First actual online capacity at the site.

Phase 2 groundbreaking (4 Jul 2023); base target raised to 41 GWh/yr (phases II & III), total investment ~13-13.5bn yuan. Announced ambition, not online. (Later English materials describe phases II+III as 36 GWh; conflict noted.)

Company IR (18 Dec 2025): Quzhou base at full production on phase-1 lines (~11 GWh online); phase-2 buildings complete, output expected 2026 with new 587Ah large-cell lines (mass delivery targeted Q3 2026). Company now frames phase 1+2 = 20 GWh total, ~6bn yuan - a more conservative figure than the 2023 41 GWh announcement.
Launch announcement: target of 2 GWh/yr annualised production rate by end of 2024 (phase 1). Never built - no capacity came online.
Launch announcement: target of 6 GWh/yr by 2026, en route to an eventual 30 GWh/yr full nameplate. Never built - project paused mid-2023, no planning application or lease.

Battery gigafactory (within Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex, Jamnagar) targeted to begin production in 2026 with an initial annual capacity of 40 GWh, modularly scalable to 100 GWh/yr. LFP chemistry, initially BESS/packs with backward integration to cell manufacturing. Announced target only — nothing operational.
Reliance raised its stated target to 120 GWh/yr of annual BESS and cell manufacturing capacity, with the first phase to start production in 2026. Headline ultimate target; not online.
Wenzhou base first cell production line commissioned (Jan 2019); no dated standalone GWh figure published for this phase.
Wenzhou base (~20 ha) annual planned/nameplate capacity reaches ~26 GWh after lines commissioned through Sep 2022.
Wenzhou Phase III (三期) groundbreaking on 2023-03-01: +24 GWh cell (plus PACK), stated to bring the Wenzhou base total to 50 GWh once operational.
IPO prospectus target: expand Wenzhou factory to ~50 GWh by end-2025 (Phase III designed 24 GWh).
Wenzhou REPT Battero plant (Phase III workshops, ~580,000 m2) passes construction completion acceptance (竣工验收), consistent with ~50 GWh site capacity built.

GM & Samsung SDI announce plan for a new US battery cell plant: >$3bn investment, 30 GWh/yr annual capacity, prismatic high-nickel plus cylindrical cells, production targeted for 2026. Site not yet chosen.

New Carlisle, St. Joseph County, Indiana chosen as the site; investment raised to ~$3.5bn; 'more than 30 GWh' annual capacity, 1,600+ jobs, production targeted for 2026. Construction site preparation begins.

JV finalised (~$3.5bn): 27 GWh/yr initial capacity scaling to 36 GWh/yr full nameplate; NCA nickel-rich prismatic cells for GM Ultium EVs; mass production pushed to 2027 (a year later than first planned).

GM & Samsung SDI PAUSE construction to align capacity with weak US EV demand (after removal of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit). No cells produced; 36 GWh/yr target and production start date now uncertain; nothing online.
Göd site (first + second plant) reported at ~30 GWh/yr annual capacity; article says it is expected to reach 'over 40 GWh' in future.
Second plant reached full production (>6 million cells/month) by January 2022; phase-2 build-out complete, bringing the combined Göd site to ~40 GWh/yr.
Site described as currently ~40 GWh/yr (enough for ~600,000 mid-size EVs) at the time of the announced renovation/expansion for prismatic stacked cells.

Announced expansion/renovation: convert first plant from wound to high-energy-density stacked cells and expand second plant, lifting total site capacity to ~60 GWh/yr (NCA stacked prismatic cells for Hyundai/Kia from 2026). Target, not yet online.

Groundbreaking of Plant 2 (SDIEM), Seremban, Negeri Sembilan. Samsung SDI committed KRW 1.7 trillion (RM5.8bn / ~USD1.3bn), phased to completion in 2025, to build cylindrical (PRiMX 21700) battery lines. Company did not officially disclose capacity; market/industry estimates cited an annual nameplate of roughly 15-20 GWh (market insiders quoted 15-16 GWh). Conservative lower-bound estimate recorded here.

Plant 2 began mass production of PRiMX 21700 cylindrical cells in 2024 as planned at groundbreaking (production-to-start-2024, completion 2025). No officially disclosed operational GWh figure; capacity remains a market estimate of ~15-20 GWh nameplate at full build-out (2025). Conservative lower-bound estimate carried to the operational point.
EV lithium-ion cell mass production begins at Ulsan (dedicated EV cell line completed Nov 2010); no GWh figure disclosed at the time
Ulsan reported producing medium-to-large-sized (EV) battery cells at ~10 GWh/yr; site is Samsung SDI's main domestic EV cell base
LFP (SBB 2.0) ESS cell line on the Ulsan 'mother line' targeted for mass production H1 2026 (South Korea's first LFP line); no site GWh figure disclosed

Groundbreaking of the Nantong lithium-battery industrial base (Nantong Economic Development Zone, 442 mu / ~200,000 sqm floor area). Total project investment RMB3bn; total planned capacity 10 GWh/yr across two phases.
Phase 1 reached full designed production (达产) on 29 Sep 2020: 5 GWh/yr cell capacity, equipment investment ~RMB1.5bn. This is the only capacity confirmed physically online.
Full two-phase design capacity is 10 GWh/yr (Phase 1 = 5 GWh online; Phase 2 = further 5 GWh). No dated source confirms Phase 2 ever being built or commissioned.

Phase I: production lines for 5 GWh/yr sodium-ion cells (plus 10,000 t cathode and 5,000 t anode materials), Phase I investment RMB1.35bn. Project record-filing (备案) completed Dec 2025; construction officially started 8 Mar 2026; construction-land planning permit pre-approval notice 16 Mar 2026; steel structure of main plant completed by ~May 2026; building completion targeted June 2026; equipment install/commissioning then trial production targeted August 2026. Nothing operational yet as of source date.

Full project ultimate design capacity: 10 GWh/yr lithium-ion + sodium-ion energy-storage cells at full build-out (Phase I + Phase II), total investment RMB5bn, sited at Shuangdeng's global HQ / new-energy-storage zero-carbon industrial park, 999 Tianmu West Road, Jiangyan Economic Development Zone. No confirmed full-nameplate completion year disclosed by the source (internal DB guess of ref-year 2027 is NOT source-confirmed).

Gemlik site began module & pack production (~3 GWh/yr) on 31 Mar 2023 using IMPORTED cells - this is NOT cell manufacturing. Foundation stone for the on-site cell factory (60 ha / ~607,000 m2) was laid 24-25 Apr 2023; local cell production targeted for 2026. No cell-making capacity online in 2023.

Battery CELL production scheduled to begin in 2026; phase-one annual cell capacity reported as ~8 GWh/yr. NOTE: sources conflict - some frame the 2026 initial phase as ~20 GWh. Conservative figure used. As of Jul 2026 no source confirms cell lines are actually operational.
Cell manufacturing capacity target of 20 GWh/yr by 2031 (announced at Apr 2023 foundation-stone ceremony).
Longer-term expansion target of more than 50 GWh/yr by 2035 (announced 2023).
Ford and SK Innovation announced BlueOval City (Stanton, TN) including a single BlueOval SK battery plant of ~43 GWh/yr; production originally targeted for mid-decade (~2025). Not operational.
Tennessee plant still specified at 43 GWh/yr; battery production timeline slipped, then targeted for 2027. Construction ongoing, not operational.

Construction completed April 2025 but plant NOT in production. Dec 2025: Ford and SK On agreed to unwind the BlueOval SK JV, with SK On taking sole ownership/operation of the Tennessee plant; battery production now slated for 2028. Capacity still cited as 43 GWh/yr.
Plant 1 (9.8 GWh) targeted to come online Q1 2022; second plant announced to bring combined site capacity to ~21.5 GWh
Plant 2 (11.7 GWh) construction to start July 2020, mass production targeted 2023, bringing the Commerce site to ~21.5 GWh combined
Plant 1 began mass production in early 2022 (9.8 GWh/yr), supplying Ford F-150 Lightning and VW ID.4 cells
Plant 2 reached mass production during 2023, taking the Commerce site to its full ~21.5 GWh/yr combined nameplate (two lithium-ion cell plants operating)
SK Innovation announces third European battery cell plant at Iváncsa, Hungary: 30 GWh/yr annual capacity, USD 2.29bn investment, production targeted for early 2024 and full site completion by ~2028.
Iváncsa plant begins mass production in Q2 2024 at 30 GWh/yr annual nameplate capacity; reaches >90% yield within three months, raising SK On's total European capacity to 47.5 GWh.
Komárom 1 groundbreaking (8 March 2018); first plant planned at 7.5 GWh/yr, NCM 811 pouch EV cells. Not yet online.
SK Innovation announces/starts construction of second Komárom plant (Komárom 2), planned ~9–10 GWh/yr. Announced, not yet online.
Komárom 1 begins mass production in Q1 2020 at 7.5 GWh/yr nameplate. First SK battery cell output online in Hungary.
Komárom 2 begins mass production in Q1 2022 (~9.8–10 GWh/yr), bringing the Komárom site total to ~16.5–17.5 GWh/yr across both plants. Site later reported running >80% utilisation.
SK (SK Innovation) establishes the Seosan battery site with an initial ~0.2 GWh/yr cell capacity
Two operating plants at Seosan producing ~5 GWh/yr; SK On's only domestic (Korean) cell site
Site operational capacity still ~5 GWh/yr; Plant 3 expansion delayed (investment completion pushed from Dec 2025 to Dec 2026), so third-line capacity not yet online
Aug 2023 KRW 1.5tn plan: third plant to quadruple Seosan capacity from ~5 GWh to ~20 GWh by 2028 (Plant 3 initial ops targeted 2025, ramping to 14 GWh) - since delayed
SKOJ Plant 1 (~10 GWh/yr) reached commercial operation in Q1 2021. This was the first of two cell plants at the Yancheng SKOJ joint-venture base (SK On ~70% / EVE Energy 30%).
SKOJ Plant 2 (~17 GWh/yr) reached commercial operation in Q3 2022, taking the Yancheng SKOJ site to ~27 GWh/yr total nameplate (Plant 1 10 GWh + Plant 2 17 GWh), enough for ~360,000 mid-size EVs.

After acquiring EVE Energy's 30% stake (completed 22 June 2026, SK On now 100% owner), SK On announced ~KRW 200bn to modify/upgrade eight existing production lines at SKOJ, with full-scale mass production targeted for 2027. No specific new GWh figure was disclosed - this is a line-conversion/upgrade, not a stated capacity addition.

Plant 1 (first StarPlus Energy Kokomo gigafactory) announced with initial 23 GWh/yr target, launch planned Q1 2025 (later raised to 33 GWh). Documented as the 'initial target of 23 GWh' in the Oct 2023 Stellantis release.

Kokomo confirmed as site for a SECOND StarPlus Energy gigafactory (Plant 2), ~34 GWh/yr, production expected early 2027, ~$3.2bn. Plant 1 target now stated at 33 GWh/yr (up from 23), opening Q1 2025. Combined two-plant nameplate target = 67 GWh/yr. (Second-plant plans first announced July 2023.)

Plant 1 began battery cell production in early 2025 (nameplate 33 GWh/yr). Detroit News reports StarPlus 'began production in Kokomo earlier this year'. Plant 2 not yet online. Year-by-year ramp not published, so 33 GWh is stated nameplate online, not confirmed full-rate output.
Plant 2 (~34 GWh/yr) targeted to begin production early 2027, bringing the combined two-plant Kokomo nameplate to 67 GWh/yr.
Project launch (April 2024): first modular production line of ~6 GWh (semi-solid-state cells) targeted fully operational by end of 2026 at Al Ghail Industrial Park, RAKEZ.

Announced full nameplate capacity of up to 40 GWh/yr once further production lines are added and the plant reaches full operation (no specific date given for full 40 GWh; only the first ~6 GWh line is tied to end-2026).

Statevolt launched by Lars Carlstrom; announced a 54 GWh lithium-ion gigafactory for Imperial Valley, California ($4bn, ~2,500 jobs, batteries for ~650,000 EVs/yr), sourcing lithium/geothermal power from Controlled Thermal Resources' Hell's Kitchen. Announcement/planning only - no site, no construction.
Statevolt acquired a 135-acre site near the Salton Sea; 54 GWh nameplate target unchanged, production still targeted for ~2025. Land acquired but no groundbreaking; nothing operational.

Strategic shift: California/Imperial Valley operations paused, company refocused on energy-storage (semi-solid) cells and a UAE (Ras Al Khaimah) plant. No groundbreaking ever occurred in Imperial Valley and no cell capacity was commissioned - real online capacity remained zero.

Sunwoda Automotive Battery (operating co. Deyang Sunwoda New Energy) signed investment agreement with Shifang municipal government to build a power & energy-storage battery cell base. Initial official figure: 20 GWh, ~CNY 8bn. Project subsequently reported at 25 GWh / ~CNY 10bn / ~700 mu.
First production line entered trial production (March 2023); line 2 equipment being installed and line 3 equipment arriving end-March — ramp beginning, full nameplate not yet online.

25 GWh power & energy-storage battery production lines reported put into production during 2023 (two lines described as fully operational within the year). A further 7.4 GWh ESS-cell line reported under construction on top of this.
Site confirmed in full production ('百日百亿' retrospective, July 2025); described as an industry-leading operational base and part of Shifang's provincial advanced-materials industry cluster.

Thailand BOI approves >US$1bn (THB ~50bn) for two Sunwoda EV/ESS battery CELL factories in Chonburi (EEC); first cell manufacturer in Thailand/ASEAN; production targeted to start 2025. No per-site GWh disclosed in approval.
Phase I trial production reported begun (subsidiary Sunwoda Power Thailand established 2024, ~US$259m invested). Phase I annual capacity in GWh not publicly disclosed.

Phase II expansion announced (29 Oct 2025): planned annual capacity 17.4 GWh/yr, investment capped at US$482m. This is a future/announced target - no confirmed operational year; possibly Phase II-only or full-site total (see hub_note).
Project announced: 50 GWh/yr total power + ESS battery base at Yiwu, Zhejiang, RMB 21.3bn, in two phases (Phase 1 30 GWh, Phase 2 20 GWh). Nothing yet built.
Groundbreaking / construction start at Yiwu Green Power Town (~4 Dec 2022). Phase 1 = 30 GWh line; 500-day build programme. No capacity online yet.

Phase 1 commissioned: first cell and pack rolled off the line on 9 Dec 2023; Phase 1 30 GWh production line put into production (supplying Geely/Volvo). Figure is the Phase 1 line nameplate at commissioning, not a separately-dated full-ramp output.

Phase 2 (20 GWh, RMB 8.5bn) environmental impact assessment accepted 21 Jul 2025 by Yiwu eco-environment bureau; would raise site total to 50 GWh/yr, completion targeted around 2026. Still at approval stage as of mid-2025, not online.

Sunwoda (via subsidiary Sunwoda Power / Xinzhiwang) signed an investment agreement with the Zhuhai municipal government (Jinwan district) on 28 Feb 2022 for a planned 30 GWh/yr power + energy-storage battery cell production base, total investment ~RMB 12bn. This is an announced target only — no capacity was ever online.

On 22 April 2025 Sunwoda announced termination of the Zhuhai 30 GWh project (one of two cancelled projects totalling ~RMB 14bn). Company stated the project had made no substantial construction progress, with only minimal early-stage investment and no further capital committed. Plant never reached construction or operation.

Announced 9 Aug 2021: Sunwoda (wholly-owned Nanchang Sunwoda) to invest RMB ~20bn in the Nanchang power battery production base, ~1,800 mu, full nameplate 50 GWh/yr of cells over four phases (phase 1: 4 GWh; phase 2: +10 GWh; phase 3: +16 GWh; phase 4: +20 GWh cells).
Phase 1 (leased Jinkai park; 4 GWh cell + 4 GWh battery-system line, ~RMB 1.6bn) reached production around April 2022. Government/company sources confirm mass production began in 2022.

As of March 2024, phases 1-3 (15 production lines built in 15 months) fully commissioned, giving 35.9 GWh/yr of power-battery capacity online at the site - described as the group's fastest-built and largest operational battery base.
Phase 4 (+20 GWh cells) planned for 2026 implementation per the original four-phase plan, taking the site to its 50 GWh/yr full nameplate. Not yet confirmed operational.

Project announced (April 2019 groundbreaking): ~12bn yuan, three phases, full-build target of 30 GWh cells + 30 GWh battery systems. Phase 1 ~8 GWh cell, Phase 2 +10 GWh, Phase 3 +12 GWh. This 30 GWh is the full-build PLAN, not online capacity.

Phase 1 factory mass-production handover ceremony held in Lishui district, Nanjing (10 July 2020). Two HEV lines and one BEV line, 4 GWh/yr power-cell capacity. This is the real online nameplate at the site.

JV announced: 30 GWh power battery base in Yichang, two phases (phase 1 = 20 GWh / RMB 8bn, phase 2 = 10 GWh / RMB 4bn), RMB 12bn total; construction started 30 Oct 2022. 30 GWh is a future target, none online yet.

Phase-1 cell line commissioned: first batch of battery cells rolled off / delivered on 10 Oct 2023 (313 days after trial production began). Phase-1 nameplate is 20 GWh/yr; figure is phase-1 line commissioning, not a confirmed fully-ramped output.

SVOLT signs agreement with Chengdu city government (Sept 2021) to build a power-battery base in Chengdu Eastern New Area (Jianzhou New Town). Announced as ~60 GWh at full nameplate, to be built in three expansion phases of 20 GWh each; total investment CNY 22bn (~EUR 2.9bn), first phase ~CNY 10bn. Nothing online yet.
Groundbreaking / foundation laid (7 Jan 2022); construction of phase 1 begins. Reported as a ~USD 1.57bn (~CNY 10bn) first-phase investment. No capacity online yet.

Phase 1 enters production (25 Oct 2023): first flying-stacked short-blade 325Ah LFP energy-storage cell rolls off the line. Official project = total investment CNY 22bn in two phases; phase 1 investment ~CNY 11.6bn with designed capacity ~31.5 GWh. Base achieved 'break ground, start production and reach scale in the same year' - SVOLT's fastest-to-production site. Figure is phase-1 design nameplate; output was still ramping.

Base declared fully operational (全面投运, 26 Oct 2024): three cell products - 325Ah and 350Ah ESS cells plus 162Ah 2nd-gen short-blade power cell - in mass production, with PACK units also produced. Phase 1 (~31.5 GWh design capacity) now fully in operation, supplying ESS customers and automakers (e.g. Geely). Phase 2 (~28.5 GWh, to reach the ~60 GWh total plan) not yet built as of this date.
Phase 2 (20 GWh/yr) groundbreaking on 16 Feb 2022 in Shangrao ETDZ; brings planned total site capacity to 24 GWh/yr (4 GWh phase 1 + 20 GWh phase 2). Phase 2 = 566 mu, 8x 16PPM lines, RMB 12.5bn.
Phase 1 (4 GWh/yr) reached full mass production ('全面量产') in December 2022.
Phase 2 (20 GWh/yr) commissioned / put into production ('竣工投产') on 26 Jul 2023, lifting total site nameplate to 24 GWh/yr.
SVOLT signs agreement (19 Feb 2021) with Huzhou city government to build a 20 GWh/yr power-battery base in South Taihu New Area; investment ~RMB 7bn, ~755 mu land.

Phase 1 reached SOP (Apr 2023); first energy-storage (222Ah) cells mass-produced and rolled off the line at the Huzhou base on 7-8 May 2023, reported as 'put into production' (投产). GWh shown is the base's design nameplate credited at commissioning (IEA/BNEF-style); no sourced phase-1-only online figure exists for this specific site.

Project signed 1 Feb 2021 / publicly announced Apr 2021: SVOLT to invest RMB 11bn on a battery cell + PACK production and R&D base in Ma'anshan (Anhui) with planned full annual capacity of 28 GWh. 28 GWh is the planned full build-out, not a confirmed online figure.

Phase 1 online: first cells rolled off the Ma'anshan line on 17 Mar 2021 (rapid start via takeover of an existing plant); cobalt-free cells in volume production at the base by end-2021. SVOLT's IPO prospectus states one Ma'anshan production line completed its capacity ramp during 2021. No site-level online GWh figure is disclosed for this online portion.

Ma'anshan operating: the ramped Ma'anshan line ran at 97.19% capacity utilisation in H1 2022 (SVOLT IPO prospectus); the Ma'anshan subsidiary reported ~RMB 0.5bn output value in H1 2022 and Ma'anshan made its first lithium-battery export in Oct 2022. Still no disclosed site-level online GWh.
Phase 1 announced: SVOLT–Suining agreement signed 2021-01-27, groundbreaking 2021-03-29; 20 GWh planned (10 cell + 9 module lines), 7.1bn yuan.
Phase 1 (20 GWh, 10 cell + 9 module lines) commissioned at ceremony on 2022-10-31; first LFP short-blade cell line live, remaining lines phased in through end-December 2022.
Phase 2 (4 additional cell lines, +9 GWh) targeted to complete line commissioning by mid-2023, taking the Suining base to a planned 29 GWh. Actual phase-2 commissioning not confirmed in sources.
Groundbreaking of the 22.3 GWh two-phase Yancheng base (RMB 10bn); Phase 1 targeted H1 2022, Phase 2 H1 2023. This 22.3 GWh is the FULL planned two-phase nameplate, not day-one online capacity.

Phase 1 online: first L400 short-blade fly-stack (飞叠) cells rolled off the line April 2022; mass-production ceremony held 3 Sep 2022; Phase 1 subsequently reported at full production. Phase-1-only GWh not disclosed by any source.

Phase 2 (9 fly-stack cell lines + 9 module/PACK lines) into trial production/commissioning from end-June 2023; ~60% of commissioning done by end June, final commissioning completing around Sep 2023. Phase-2-only GWh not disclosed.
Full two-phase base (~22.3 GWh/yr nameplate, cited as 23 GWh) reported operating at full capacity; Phase 1 at full production and Phase 2 fully commissioned/in production.

Phase 1 (4 GWh) of SVOLT's first automotive-grade AI intelligent battery cell plant in Jintan, Changzhou officially opened 27 Nov 2019; line reached SOP (start of production) Feb 2020. Total three-phase site plan = 18 GWh (4+8+6) on ~800 mu, ~RMB8bn investment.

As of February 2021 the first Jintan cell factory had 12 GWh/yr of manufacturing capacity operational (Phase 1 4 GWh + Phase 2 8 GWh). NMx cobalt-free cathode pilot completed Jan 2021 at this site; cobalt-free NMX cell series production launched here July 2021.

Phase 3 (6 GWh, alongside a cathode-material line) built out the original three-phase Jintan factory to its full 18 GWh/yr nameplate. Reported commissioning timing conflicts across sources (Feb/Aug 2022 in one construction notice; Jan 2023 in another); 18 GWh total is the well-established full nameplate for this site.
Project signed with Nanjing Lishui development zone: LFP power-battery production base, 14.6 GWh planned total, ~5.6bn yuan, two phases (phase 1 6.6 GWh, phase 2 8 GWh).

Phase 1: 2 of 4 LFP cell lines entered trial production (May 2022); cumulative production output reported at 1.086 GWh (output, not nameplate). Phase-1 nameplate not separately stated by source (~half of eventual 8.94 GWh).

Phase 2 (2 more cell lines) supply-capable March 2023; all 4 LFP cell lines completed and in trial production by July 2023 — full built cell capacity 8.94 GWh/yr (plus 6 module/PACK lines). Corroborated by 2nd-gen L600 196Ah short-blade cell rolling off the Nanjing line on 2023-05-04.
Tangshan Guoxuan Battery Co. established Aug 2016; phase 1 line (~1 GWh) commissioned (phase split per trade-press recap of company announcement 2019-074 - medium confidence)
Phase 2 (~2 GWh) added, bringing existing Tangshan capacity to ~3 GWh - the 'existing 3 GWh' cited in the Nov 2019 expansion announcement (phase-year split is medium confidence)

18 Nov 2019 framework agreement: RMB 5.5bn 'Guoxuan 5G new-energy base' adding 7 GWh to expand existing 3 GWh to 10 GWh; construction to finish Q3 2021 and commission by end-2021 (target, not confirmed operational)
Tangshan base capacity reported at ~20 GWh from prior projects ('先期项目') as of early 2025, before the new heavy-truck cell project

New 10 GWh heavy-duty NEV (truck) cell project (RMB 3.5bn, 159.2 mu); provincial approval 23 Jan 2025, groundbreaking late Feb 2025 via 'land-and-build'; company said Oct 2025 trial production would raise total Tangshan site capacity to 30 GWh

First 4680 cell production begins at Giga Texas. First production cells shown at Cyber Rodeo (Apr 2022); Tesla targeted starting volume 4680 cell production in Q3 2022 and exceeding the Kato (Fremont) pilot line's weekly output by year-end. No GWh nameplate published.

20 millionth 4680 cell produced at Giga Texas (10M added in ~4 months). Run rate ~600k cells/week, ~80 MWh/week, i.e. roughly 4-5 GWh/yr annualised online capacity; described as enough for ~25,000 Cybertrucks/yr. GWh figure is a press conversion of the cell run-rate, not an official nameplate.

Tesla reports producing 4680 cells for >1,000 Cybertruck packs per week at Giga Texas (~123 MWh/week, ~6 GWh/yr annualised run rate). Q1 2024 4680 output up ~18-20% vs Q4 2023 (Lars Moravy). Annualised run-rate conversion, not official nameplate.

100 millionth 4680 cell produced at Giga Texas (14-15 Sep 2024), ~3 months after the 50-millionth (6 Jun 2024). Reported annualised run rate ~17.2 GWh/yr, with estimates of ~20 GWh/yr as the rate rose (~495k cells/day). Best real-world estimate of online single-site 4680 capacity in late 2024 - far below the ~100 GWh in the current DB record. Annualised run-rate conversion, not official nameplate.

Long-term aspirational target: Giga Texas 4680 cell manufacturing scaling towards ~100 GWh/yr (mid-2024 100 GWh/yr 4680 run-rate ambition). This is an unbuilt target and is frequently conflated with Tesla's SEPARATE $3.6bn Giga Nevada 100 GWh 4680 project; it likely reflects a company-wide 4680 aspiration rather than confirmed Texas nameplate. Flagged - do not treat as online capacity.
Musk announced Berlin would become the world's largest battery cell plant, initial capacity 'up to 100 GWh', possibly rising to 200-250 GWh. Aspirational, no firm year; project put on hold in 2022.
Tesla revived cell plans (after 2022 hold) with an initial target of 8 GWh/yr, cell production to start in 2027; ~EUR 1bn total investment in the cell unit.
Pilot 4680 cell line reportedly produced its first cells (~12 May 2026); this is pilot/ramp only, no nameplate annual GWh online.
Tesla raised the cell capacity target from 8 to 18 GWh/yr via an additional $250M investment; full-scale production targeted for H1 2027, +1,500 jobs.

Groundbreaking / project launch (26 June 2022) at Binhai Hi-Tech Zone: 24 GWh EV power-battery base planned, ~RMB10bn investment, three phases of 8 GWh each, all to be completed within four years; Phase 1 (8 GWh) targeted for completion and start of production in 2023. Announced target, not confirmed online.

Groundbreaking / commencement ceremony (8 Feb 2022). Announced total ~36 GWh/yr of power + energy-storage cells, ~RMB 15.2bn investment, in three phases; phase 1 planned at 16 GWh with target operation in H1 2023. Nothing online yet at this date.

Base formally put into production at commissioning ceremony on 27 Oct 2023. Phase 1 = 22 GWh/yr online (8 GWh power cells + 14 GWh energy-storage cells), built from June 2022 construction start. First vehicle battery packs off the line confirmed Dec 2023.

Full planned base scaled up to 48 GWh/yr total. Phase 2 (20 GWh/yr energy-storage cells) signed at the Oct 2023 ceremony, construction targeted for H1 2024. No dated source confirms phase 2 actually operational; only the 22 GWh phase 1 is confirmed online.
Project settled/signed in Xishan District, Wuxi. ~11.2bn yuan investment; 24 GWh/yr lithium battery base planned in two 12 GWh phases.
Construction started (groundbreaking 28 Jun 2022) in Ehu Town, Xishan, Wuxi. Phase 1 = 12 GWh LFP power-cell lines; phase-1 production targeted for 2023. Nothing yet online.
Phase 1 main structural works topped out (~Nov 2023); still pre-production. No confirmed operational capacity.
As of Jul 2024 some phase-1 production lines in equipment installation and trial production. Trial production only; no confirmed nameplate GWh online.

March 2022: Zhejiang Tianneng New Energy announces a 15 GWh/yr energy-storage + power lithium battery base at South Taihu Industrial Cluster, Changxing sub-district (Huzhou); three phases, ~CNY 5.17bn, 583 mu of new land, 10 automated cell + PACK lines. Nothing online yet (target).

2 Nov 2023: Phase 1 of the Changxing South Taihu lithium battery base commissioned, reported at 6 GWh/yr cell + PACK capacity (first-phase investment ~CNY 3bn). This is the physical commissioning milestone.

IPO-funded 'Huzhou South Taihu base 10 GWh/yr lithium battery project', implemented by Tianneng New Energy (Huzhou) Co., Ltd. (~CNY 3.97bn): phase 1 = 3 GWh LFP, phase 2 = 7 GWh LFP. As of 31 Oct 2025 phase 1 fully built and meeting targets and phase 2 core production lines completed and operational (88.72% of capex deployed); full-project 'expected usable state' date extended to Dec 2027.
Phase 1 (10 GWh/yr) officially put into production on 8 Aug 2022; phase 2 broke ground the same day.
Announced total planned capacity 40 GWh/yr across three phases (phase 1 10 GWh, phase 2 20 GWh, phase 3 10 GWh).
By Dec 2023 Tongcheng base capacity reported at 30 GWh: phase 2 first batch 10 GWh already producing (~20 GWh online) plus a further 10 GWh under equipment installation.

Plant announced for Liberty, NC (Toyota + Toyota Tsusho JV, later Toyota Battery Manufacturing North Carolina). Initial $1.29bn investment; capacity described in production lines/vehicles, not a stated GWh figure.

Site physically commissioned. Production began 2025 (HEV module shipments from ~April/June 2025); officially 'powered on' 12 Nov 2025 with 3 of 14 planned lines running and a 4th being installed. No source quantifies the GWh actually online at this point (line count only), so cumulative online GWh is left null rather than derived from the line count.
Full-nameplate target of more than 30 GWh/yr across all 14 production lines; additional lines set to launch through 2030. Total investment ~$13.9bn (built up via 2022 and Oct-2023 $8bn expansions).

12 GWh/yr LFP energy-storage cell project (3 LFP cell lines + 2 assembly lines, RMB4.5bn) lands/signed in Chuzhou Economic & Technological Development Zone; 12 GWh cell nameplate planned. Not yet built.

Chuzhou cell+system super-factory enters production in 2023; ~12 GWh cell delivery capability built by year-end 2023 (site visit Nov 2023). Base described as 12 GWh cell / 6 GWh PACK / 16 GWh integration.
Chuzhou base cell capacity still 12 GWh/yr (3 LFP cell lines); confirmed in Aug 2025 manufacturing update.

Chuzhou Ecology & Environment Bureau EIA acceptance (22 Jun 2026) for new 36 GWh mass-production cell + 1 GWh pilot-cell R&D project (RMB7.2bn); on completion Chuzhou base cell capacity planned to rise to 48 GWh/yr. Future target, not yet online.
GM and LG Energy Solution announce $2.3bn second US Ultium Cells plant in Spring Hill, TN, with 35 GWh/yr nameplate; construction to begin immediately, opening targeted for late 2023.
Ultium Cells announces additional $275m investment to expand Spring Hill nameplate capacity by ~40%, from 35 to 50 GWh/yr, when fully operational.
Spring Hill begins battery cell production (March 2024); first pouch cells shipped to GM (Cadillac Lyriq). Plant online at 35 GWh/yr, ramping toward the 50 GWh/yr target.
GM and LG Energy Solution announce Ultium Cells JV (5 Dec 2019); Lordstown plant planned at 'more than 30 GWh' annual capacity, ~$2.3bn investment.
Groundbreaking May 2020; construction of the ~30+ GWh, 2.8m sq ft cell plant begins.
Battery cell production begins August 2022; plant ramping (~20% of capacity added per quarter) toward full nameplate. No GWh-online figure stated at start.
GM Q3 2023 earnings: Warren/Lordstown plant operating at ~75% of full capacity.
GM Q4 2023 earnings: plant reached 100% of full nameplate capacity by end of Q4 2023. Full nameplate recorded conservatively at 35 GWh/yr (sources range 30–40 GWh).
Verkor selects Dunkirk for its first gigafactory; 16 GWh/yr initial planned for 2025, expandable to 50 GWh by 2030
Foundation stone laid / construction start (16 Nov 2023); €2bn financing package secured Sept 2023 to launch 16 GWh/yr phase 1
Gigafactory inaugurated 11 Dec 2025 with initial nameplate capacity of 16 GWh/yr; production begins (first commercial deliveries 2026, Alpine A390)
Company target to scale the site from 16 GWh to 50 GWh/yr by 2030

Volklec to begin cell production on UKBIC's existing 100 MWh (0.1 GWh/yr) line in Coventry - 21700 cylindrical NMC 'energy cell'. Start planned for later in 2025 (announcement, not yet confirmed operational).
Additional 1 GWh 'power cell' production line to be installed at UKBIC by end of 2026 (in addition to the 100 MWh energy-cell line), bringing site capacity to ~1.1 GWh/yr.
Roadmap targets a dedicated 10 GWh gigafactory (£1bn, ~1,000 jobs) by the end of the decade / 2030. Location of the dedicated facility not confirmed at announcement.

Waaree Energies announced (Feb 2026) an integrated greenfield lithium-ion gigafactory at Rambilli, Anakapalli district, Andhra Pradesh — 16 GWh covering the full value chain including cell manufacturing, packs and BESS; investment ₹8,175 crore; in-principle approval from the AP State Investment Promotion Board; targeted to be commissioned and fully operational by July 2027. No construction start confirmed as of mid-2026.
Wanxiang announces an 80 GWh/yr battery cell factory in Hangzhou (part of Wanxiang Innovation Energy City), ~160 ha site, ~USD 10bn investment. Full nameplate target, not online.

Construction of Wanxiang Innovation Energy City officially breaks ground (Xiaoshan, Hangzhou), March 2019. Battery base total plan 80 GWh/yr (17 two-storey UNIT buildings, ~68bn yuan); construction period stated as 2019-2035. Nothing online yet.

Phase 1 24 GWh factory building completed and the first 3.85 GWh/yr production line officially put into production on 28 March 2024 (first cells off the line). Phase 2 (32 GWh) only in preliminary design. Only 3.85 GWh actually online, not 80 GWh.
Investor site note (13 Oct 2024): Energy City base planned at 80 GWh but only 3.85 GWh built/online to date; utilisation low. Confirms the 3.85 GWh figure held through late 2024.
Project launched/groundbreaking (Nov 2023): three-phase Weichai-FinDreams (Yantai) New Energy Power Industrial Park, RMB 5.6bn, planned 50 GWh/yr cell base (+50 GWh/yr pack) at full build.
Phase 1 commissioned 28 March 2025 - first blade battery cell off the line. Phase 1 = 20 GWh/yr cell capacity (plus a separate 20 GWh/yr pack line) using FinDreams 2.0 blade-cell equipment.

BYD/FinDreams announces new power-battery base in Qiaotou town, Yongjia county, Wenzhou; planned annual capacity 20 GWh, total investment RMB 6.5bn, first production line expected to start in 2024. Nothing online yet. Wenzhou FinDreams Battery Co., Ltd. established 2022-12-09.

Construction of the Wenzhou battery base officially starts (groundbreaking). Planned annual capacity 20 GWh, total investment RMB 6.5bn; first production line still expected in 2024. No capacity online yet.

Nov 2024 Wenzhou FinDreams environmental impact report states the plant has been 'built and put into operation' (已建成投产), forming 20 GWh/yr annual NEV power-battery (blade/LFP) capacity, with formal project acceptance still pending. A parallel 2024 Wenzhou 'Hundred Projects, Hundred Billion' major-projects list (Wen Zheng Fa [2024] No.8, 2023-2026 build period) describes phase 1 in production and phase 2 main structure still under construction - so the full 20 GWh may not all have been physically online in 2024. Conservative single operational figure recorded; moderate confidence.

Gotion High-tech board announcement (No. 2025-050) to invest up to RMB 4.0004bn in the 20 GWh/year Wuhu Gotion New Energy Battery Base in the Wuhu Economic & Technological Development Zone, Anhui. Full nameplate target of 20 GWh/year; construction period up to 24 months from commencement. This is the announced target, NOT capacity online.
Phase 1 line reached 2.5 GWh of online cell capacity (of 14 GWh Phase 1 plan) as of Nov 2016; Phase 1 began production July 2015.
~4 GWh power-battery cell capacity operational at the Wuhu Tianyi plant.
Announced 2018 target to reach 20 GWh total capacity by 2020 via Phase 2 expansion. TARGET NOT MET (only ~6 GWh online by 2023).
~6 GWh combined power + energy-storage cell capacity operational.
Planned expansion to 12 GWh in 2024 (against a stated ~15 GWh full nameplate ambition for the site).

Yaoning (Geely-backed) announces a two-phase battery cell plant at Jianhu (Shanggang), Jiangsu; ~10.23bn yuan investment, 12 GWh full planned nameplate. Phase-1 6 GWh line began construction Dec 2022.
Phase-1 6 GWh LFP mass-production line commissioned (通线投料) on 15 Oct 2023, producing first-gen S+ LFP cells. Civil works completed end-Sep 2023.
Site in full production from May 2024 at ~100% utilisation (per Jianhu county government, Feb 2025); Shanggang base = 450 mu, phased 6 GWh + 6 GWh.
A new (third) production line targeted online by mid-2025, advancing the site toward its 12 GWh two-phase (6+6) full nameplate. Third line reported into production in 2025.
Phase I 10 GWh EV battery line put into operation on 30 May 2022 (site's first cell capacity online).

Phase II 20 GWh project (RMB 5.15bn / 51.5亿元) construction started Jan 2024; target lifts the base to 30 GWh total. NOT yet online at this date — Phase II still under construction; only Phase I's 10 GWh was operational.
Phase II 20 GWh into production Aug 2025; full-operation unveiling ceremony held 30 Nov 2025, bringing the base to 30 GWh/yr cell + PACK.
Quzhou Jidian cell plant construction started July 2022; Phase 1 planned at 24 GWh/yr, built in ~15 months
Phase 1 (24 GWh/yr) commissioned; Golden Brick 800V LFP cell production began ~Nov 2023 after ~15-month build
As of Oct 2024 Phase 1 (24 GWh/yr) operational and Phase 2 installed/ramping; utilisation still being raised, Phases 3 & 4 not yet decided
Full planned power-cell nameplate 48 GWh/yr (4 phases) plus separate 17 GWh ESS line; only Phases 1 & 2 in production as of Oct 2024, so 48 GWh is a target not yet online

Groundbreaking 27 Sep 2023 in Nanhu, Jiaxing. Full project planned at 20 GWh/yr sodium-ion cell+module capacity (+1.5 GWh/yr Li-ion module), two phases; Phase 1 = 4 GWh/yr sodium-ion cell+module. Nothing online yet.

Phase 1: 4 GWh/yr sodium-ion cell+module capacity (plus 1.5 GWh/yr Li-ion module) registered and coded as operational in Nanhu, Jiaxing; first-phase 4 GWh investment CNY1.125bn (~US$157m), ~75% equipment.

Groundbreaking 19-20 Nov 2023 on Zoolnasm's (Zhongna Energy / 众钠能源) Guangde 'Xunna' sodium-ion cell base, Anhui (RMB 10bn, ~600 mu). Full site planned 20 GWh sodium-ion cells + 10 GWh systems in two phases. Phase 1 = 10 GWh cells (~323 mu, RMB 4bn), targeted completion Aug 2024 with capacity release by end-2024. Announced target only.

Phase 1 10 GWh cell capacity was targeted to be released by end-2024 per the Nov-2023 groundbreaking announcement. NO dated source found confirming actual commissioning / operational cell output at Guangde; company's confirmed 2025-26 production activity is at other bases (Yancheng pilot; Meishan). Treat as planned, not online.
